After toasting and lighting the cigar with a soft, double-flame lighter, the first few draws produce a smorgasbord of aromas and flavors, which melds into palate-coating deliciousness. Soon thereafter, a tingle on the tip of the tongue develops—which is indicative of the Piloto tobacco used in the binder and the filler. As the robusto settles into the burn, Davidoff’s characteristic mustiness begins to flirt in and out of the profile. These initial notes blend toward a mouthwatering flavor profile that proceeds in a linear fashion from the front of the tongue to the rear of the palate. Flavors and aromas of cedar, espresso, and pecans mingle together in a heavenly balance. The retrohale is piquant and smooth—hardwoods and white pepper—and is an essential component in the enjoyment of this cigar (See “ How To Retrohale a Cigar ”). An excellent open draw produces a rather prodigious amount of smoke output. As the Davidoff 702 Series Special “R” enters into its second third, the strength settles into the medium range, while the body of the cigar becomes smooth and round. The Rocky Patel Gold Label is now available in Germany for selected specialist retailers via the German importer M. K. & Söhne. Gold Label lives up to its name: gold was used in abundance for the elegant box and the opulent belly band – a design characterized by filigree ornaments and an imposing appearance. Inspired by Rocky Patel’s Indian roots, the visual appearance underlines the luxurious character of this cigar line. The exquisite tobacco blend begins with a shiny Ecuador H-2000 wrapper. Two Connecticut tobaccos are used for the binder – Broadleaf and Shade, which provide a gentle yet expressive structure. The aromatic core is formed by the long-matured filler made from premium tobaccos from Jalapa and Estelí, two of Nicaragua’s most renowned tobacco-growing regions. »Rocky had this blend in his drawer for a long time,« explains Nish Patel, Executive Vice President of the company. »He wanted something with a lot of flavor – I think Gold Label has just that. It’s very smooth, very balanced, just a well-rounded smoke.« Despite its classy appearance, Gold Label remains surprisingly accessible in price: it ranges from €8.90/each to €17/each, making it the ideal choice for everyday luxury enjoyment. It is available in four formats: Half Corona, Robusto, Toro and Sixty. . Rocky Patel Cigars and its German importer, M. K. & Söhne, announce the gradual transition of the popular Vintage Series 1990 to box-pressed formats. This change will replace the round formats, which were previously rolled exclusively for the German market. The Robusto will lead the way and is already being delivered in the box-pressed format. This step responds to the increasing popularity of box-pressed cigars. However, Rocky Patel is going beyond merely following a trend. The box-pressed shape aligns with the original concept of the cigar, and Rocky is confident that the carefully balanced blend of the Vintage Series 1990 offers even better aroma development in the box-pressed format. This decision once again highlights Rocky Patel’s uncompromising attention to detail and his constant drive to improve even successful products. »The Vintage Series 1990 is a bestseller in our portfolio, and we always strive to provide our customers with the best possible taste experience,« explains Rocky Patel. »The box-pressed variant enhances the complex flavors of the Vintage Series 1990 and underscores our commitment to the highest quality.« M. K. & Söhne, importer and partner of Rocky Patel in Germany, welcomes this decision: »Box-pressed formats are enjoying growing popularity in the German market, and the Vintage Series 1990 is a top seller in our range. We are confident that the box-pressed version will continue the success story of the Vintage Series 1990.«

note_sources.text: White Label Crafted in our very own factory in Esteli, Nicaragua, this incredible medium-bodied cigar showcases a stunning Connecticut wrapper with a flavor profile so bold, every artist is sure to have their own interpretation. Featuring an iconic complexity, this flawless stick offers rich notes of cedar, cream, and an undeniably sweet finish that lingers long after its buttery bouquet has dissipated.

For over 10 years Rocky Patel tried to find the perfect name and brand to go along with this amazing composition of Nicaragua’s finest, when it dawned on him that no design or label would ever truly showcase the complexities hidden within. True inspiration can only come from a place of artistic expression — that’s when Rocky had an epiphany: the White Label. Nothing captures the possibility and spirit of craftsmanship like the image of a blank canvas. Nor does anything more aptly represent opportunity like this rare piece of art. Every smoke begins with a delicate first stroke, inviting aficionados to become artists. You never know where your work will take you; every journey will be unique and entirely your own. But no matter how you enjoy it, it will always end up a masterpiece. Crafted in Rocky Patel’s Tavicusa factory in Estelí, Nicaragua, this medium-bodied cigar showcases a stunning Connecticut wrapper with a flavor profile so bold, every artist is sure to have their own interpretation. Featuring an iconic complexity, this flawless stick offers rich notes of cedar, cream, and an undeniably sweet finish that lingers long after its buttery bouquet has dissipated. Everything from its white leather case to its rose gold interior, are immaculately crafted and meticulously bespoke. Rocky Patel: “To put it plainly, we’ve never created a cigar with a more breathtaking palette than the all-new White Label by Rocky Patel… It’s as simple as that.” Robusto 5 x 50 Toro 6 ½ x 52 Churchill 7 x 48 Sixty 6 x 60

The Rocky Patel “Year of the Horse” has officially arrived at select retailers. This limited-edition release is handcrafted in Nicaragua. A dark San Andrés wrapper surrounds a Nicaraguan binder and a blend of Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers. The company is incredibly proud of this release and excited for cigar smokers across the country (USA) to experience it finally. Cigar Talk with Rocky Patel: In this new episode of Cigar Talk, Rocky answers one of the biggest questions in premium cigars — which country produces the best tobacco? From Nicaragua and Honduras to Ecuador, Cameroon, Brazil, Connecticut, and the Dominican Republic, Rocky walks through how each region contributes something unique to a cigar blend. He explains how different soils, climates, and tobacco varietals shape flavor, strength, sweetness, spice, and aroma — and why great blending is about harmony, not just origin. For anyone interested in cigar education, tobacco growing, blending, wrappers, fillers, and the craftsmanship behind premium handmade cigars, this is an episode you won’t want to miss. My initial impression is that this is a unique cigar, as the wrapper smells like the shoreline of a lake: slightly fishy, muddy, and with hints of algae. This isn’t unpleasant, and comes across as an interesting version of earthiness and/or barnyard. I struggle to discern flavors in the cold draw, but notice some Froot Loops and light cedar creaminess. The cigar doesn’t stray from interesting/unique upon lighting, and the first flavors to cross my palate are that of sweet cherry tomatoes! Aside from that, there’s the cedar that is initially close to being the dominant flavor. The draw is perfection, but the lightness in the bunch is evident in how fast the first third flys by, clocking in at just over 13 minutes. The ash isn’t the same perfect, dense stacks that come when smoking a Melanio, but instead are puffy and flakey. Flavor and body are sub-medium at this point. Flavors pick up going into the second third, with layers of baking spices and creaminess. Like a rich chai custard, I notice tingling ginger, cinnamon, and cardamom. The ginger quickly turns up the tingle as it cruises into Spicyville. Spice, in cigars, can mean a lot of things: peppercorn, chile peppers, baking spices, etc.—this is like the burn of a strong ginger beer. Aside from these flavors, and their pleasant meshing, there isn’t a ton of complexity to be had at this point. The flavor has been bumped up into medium at this point, with the ginger and a punchy cedar note, while strength is still below the Mendoza line. The burn line is still impeccable. This cigar is racing by like Lightning McQueen—33 minutes heading into the last third. I’m really enjoying this vitola, as the Sumatra wrapper’s presence is a big part of the unique flavor profile and really shines at this ratio. A savory note joins the fresh, pungent, spicy ginger and creamy cedar, with a lingering finish of butterscotch candy sweetness. There’s something that I’m looking for, some elusive flavor, that I just can’t pinpoint. This, and the general uniqueness of the cigar, really keep me puffing away with interest. This isn’t very complex, nor are there the sort of flavor transitions that evolve and keep one intrigued, yet I just can’t help feeling increasingly tantalized as the blend moves on. The creamy-sweet, ginger-spicy, cedar-savory mixture reminds me of Thai grilled shrimp. And as soon as I think the word “Thai,” that elusive something I was searching for comes across as that “king of fruits,” the mighty durian in custard form. As I get into the last inch, the cream and cedar are the biggest things happening. The nub starts to get soft and warm, so I set it down at the one-hour mark ON THE DOT. Strength made a valiant effort to reach medium.

Drew Estate Cigars is introducing the first-ever Lancero size for both the BLACKENED M81 and BLACKENED S84 cigars—a 7 x 40 vitola . ​Each Lancero expression will be limited in production and presented in 15-count boxes, making this drop an instant collectible for fans of both the M81’s bold Maduro-on-Maduro-on-Maduro profile and the S84’s refined, yet electrifying Connecticut Shade experience. ​“This new Lancero is a guitar solo in cigar form,” says Jonathan Drew, Founder and President of Drew Estate. “It’s long, lean, and delivers deep, concentrated flavor from foot to head. The M81 Lancero slaps with rich, dark, and heavy notes, while the S84 Lancero is like a clean intro riff—smooth, creamy, and soulful—but with that metallic edge.” ​Originally created in collaboration with Metallica’s James Hetfield, BLACKENED’s Master Distiller Rob Dietrich, and Drew Estate, the BLACKENED cigar line has become a sensation among cigar lovers and metalheads alike. The M81’s triple Maduro blend – Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, Maduro binder, and Maduro long-fillers from Nicaragua and Pennsylvania – offers a dark, earthy powerhouse. ​ Meanwhile, the S84, with its Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper and a rich mix of Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler, brings a bright, complex flavor profile with plenty of attitude. ​“The Lancero format showcases the blend in a way no other size can,” explains Dietrich. “You get this incredible ratio of wrapper to filler, making every puff more rich, more refined. It’s raw, real, and unapologetically bold – just like BLACKENED.” ​The BLACKENED Lancero M81 and S84 will be available beginning August 2025 at participating Drew Diplomat Program retailers, while supplies last. ​Product Details: ​• Name: BLACKENED M81 Lancero / BLACKENED S84 Lancero ​• Size: 7 x 40 Lancero ​• Packaging: 15-count boxes ​• Availability: Limited Release ​• Release Date: 2025 ​• Retail Channels: All Channels

Drew Estate announces the rebranding of the Herrera Esteli flagship brand, as well as the national release of the Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro and Herrera Esteli Miami. The entire, updated Herrera Esteli brand will be displayed in Drew Estate’s Booth at the IPCPR Convention and Tradeshow, held July 14-17, 2018 in Las Vegas Nevada. The Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro features a dense Plantation Grown Mata Fina wrapper, over a Connecticut River Valley Broadleaf binder with fillers from Nicaragua. Manufactured at La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate, the Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro was blended by Willy Herrera is presented in 5 vitolas: Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Robusto Grande 5 ¼ x 52 MSRP $227.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Toro Especial 6 x 52 MSRP $241.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Lonsdale 6 x 44 MSRP $231.94/Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Fino 6 x 52 MSRP $269.94/ Box of 25 Herrera Esteli Brazilian Maduro Short Corona Gorda 5 7/8 x 46 MSRP $203.94/ Box of 25 The Herrera Esteli Miami is crafted by level 9 rollers from Cuba at the El Titan de Bronze on Calle Ocho in Little Havana, Miami, – Willy Herrera’s Family Factory and the oldest remaining Fabrica in Little Havana. Like the Short Corona size featured at the 2016 IPCPR Tradeshow, the complete Herrera Esteli Miami line is expertly crafted with a lavish Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over a rich Ecuadorian Sumatran binder with select fillers from the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua. The new look of Herrera Esteli Miami features a black and gold color tone and is only available to Drew Diplomat Retailers in the following 5 vitolas: Herrera Esteli Miami Robusto Grande 5×50 MSRP $109.97/ Box of 10 Herrera Esteli Miami Toro Especial 6×52 MSRP $117.47/ Box of 10 Herrera Esteli Miami Lonsdale Deluxe 6.5×44 MSRP $112.97/ Box of 10 Herrera Esteli Miami Piramide Fino 6.5×54 MSRP $127.47/ Box of 10 Herrera Esteli Miami Short Corona Gorda 5 3/4 x 48 MSRP $97.97/ Box of 10 From Little Havana, Willy Herrera, Master Blender of Drew Estate, “The Herrera Brazilian Maduro is my expression of the floral and earthy Brazilian Mata Fina tobacco. We use it typically as a binder or accent tobacco in the filler but I wanted to showcase its dynamic and unique texture. I really like the black and gold color tone of the Herrera Esteli Miami and how it fits into the brand portfolio with multiple vitola expressions in the Miami blend. Working with my family on this brand takes me back to my blending roots and sincerely excites me.” The Herrera Esteli Habano and Herrera Esteli Norteno are receiving a new look for IPCPR 2018. Each will be presented in unified Herrera Esteli Branding and will now be packaged in 25 count boxes. Willy Herrera adds, “The uniform packaging for the Herrera Esteli line has elements of classic Cuban inspired branding mixed with modern simplicity. Nica Rustica Adobe, the second expression in Drew Estate’s value-priced Nica Rustica line, is now shipping to retailers nationwide. Introduced during the May 12 broadcast of “Freestyle Live: Special Edition,” and previewed by guests at the DE25 Exclusive Pre-Party event before the Florida Barn Smoker, Nica Rustica Adobe brings to life the soul of the lively and romantic barrios and colorful colonial houses of Estelí, Nicaragua, home to La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate. While similar to the Nica Rustica Connecticut Broadleaf expression, Nica Rustica Adobe is spicier, made from a Habano wrapper, Brazilian binder and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos from Estelí and Jalapa. Available in three sizes: Toro (6 x 52), Robusto (5 x 54) and Gordo (6 x 60), Nica Rustica Adobe is packaged in 25-count boxes that are adorned with colorful original artwork designed by Subculture Studios, which captures Estelí’s rugged, robust and rustic character. Nica Rustica Adobe’s artwork also features Estelí’s official symbol, El Brujito, an estimated 6,000-year-old petroglyph of a native shaman that was discovered on a rock atop a mountain near the city. Now available at retailers nationwide, Nica Rustica Adobe presents an excellent value for all premium cigar lovers, from beginners to aficionados. o the beautiful triple cap and give a light tug on the cigar. The pre-draw is of aged tobacco with a citrusy, dark berry fruitiness . The draw is easy. I toast up, and as I’ve always said (starting right now), Pepin puts the “pep” in pepper! There is a blast of pepper, with cedar and leather, billowing in a cloud of chalky white smoke and a finish that lingers in the back of my throat – a great first draw! The flavors continue to be what I would describe as “traditional” aged tobacco , cedar , leather , earthy , and of course, pepper . The smoke is full of texture, probably the most texture I’ve ever experienced in a cigar. It coats my entire palate and lingers for minutes on end. The La Antiguedad is a slow burning, long lasting cigar. I’m able to really enjoy each puff and let the cigar rest for a few minutes at a time. The flavors build up in my mouth, so I’m pairing it with an unsweetened iced tea, and surprisingly it works really well. I’m about an hour in at this point and just passed halfway. It has required one relight and some minor touch ups. The flavors are consistent and still dominant. It is medium to full in body , leaning on the full side, and the strength is a perfect medium . Finishing up now and the cigar has yet to disappoint me, the flavors stay prominent with each draw and the retrohale has been nothing short of spectacular. Smoke billows the entire duration, it is a satisfying smoke and I am left feeling at peace. Sometimes I smoke a cigar that is great but I’m left in want of another one. This cigar is a “one and done” in a good way! Would I smoke this cigar again? Yes, most definitely. The price is right and the flavors are there—while it’s not the most interesting cigar in the MF lineup, I’d recommend buying 5-10 of these for your humidor. Short Link: My Father Cigars La Antiguedad Be sure to eat your Wheaties before smoking the La Antiguedad, because it is a long, luxurious smoke and you will need your stamina. I must mention, I did smoke the bigger 6" x 60 and was not as impressed. I believe the wrapper plays a lot to the flavors in this cigar. I highly recommend smoking the robusto size first to experience this cigar's optimum performance before experimenting with other vitolas. Pre-light aroma from the foot is straight-up brownie batter, giving way to some cigarette tobacco aroma, followed by a leathery chemical smell. The cold draw offers sensations of sweetness, more of that brownie batter; not much else. As I toast the cigar, the girth, excessive labels, and box-press make it feel clunky and unwieldy—I almost drop it several times as I try to roll it over the soft flame. Smoke output starts out pretty heavy, despite the draw being a touch (or two) looser than what I would like; akin to drinking root beer through a straw with a hole in it, rather than a drinking a milkshake. I used a v-cut, as larger ring gauges with box-press seem to smoke pretty well that way (guillotine-style cutters can occasionally damage pressed cigars, as the square shape of the cigar is met with the rounded blade). Initial flavors are of coffee, black pepper, heavy doses of cedar, and cinnamon bark (to be differentiated from the more pleasant, ground cinnamon flavor). Ten minutes or so in and the pepper has faded into the mix—pretty on-par for a MF release. I’m blasting through this cigar pretty quickly; the light draw starts to seem kind of airy, and after 21 minutes, I move into the second third. Body is not quite medium (I hope it makes it that far), with flavor and strength not far ahead, although they are at least asking to be let into the building where medium resides… The second third brings a pretty enjoyable chocolate shortbread flavor, which is the first hint of the gooey, sweet flavors from the cold draw. Cinnamon has transitioned from the tannic, herbal, medicinal tree bark flavor of the first third into the more pleasant baking spice realm. The mild black pepper sits right on the back of the tongue. Some mild anise and licorice root join the fold (think those little candy-coated fennel seeds you get at Indian restaurants). I feel more like I’m picking flavors out of the ether, than deciphering a palate-full experience. I’m looking, reaching, waiting for the cigar to really present itself. The cigar’s airy draw is really holding it back, I think. Opulence (in reference to the cigar’s title) is typically used to describe extravagance, lavishness, richness; whereas the experience speaks more towards elegance, refinement, or restraint. It’s certainly tasteful, but I was expecting more of a big, chewy, full-bodied experience. The robusto does begin to gain traction, but still not even into medium territory, as the second third closes after a much-improved 35 minutes. Into the final third, the cigar is not as light, both in terms of smoke production and flavor. The draw has firmed up a little, and the spiciness is coming back into the picture. This is more along the lines of what I had expected. There’s big coffee flavor, some creaminess, black tea with garden mint, even a little raspberry jam to kick in some sweetness. There is lots of cocoa going into the final inch, backed by nutty brown butter. Finishing with spice and anise, this cigar completes its nearly two-hour journey into finally reaching medium strength and body, with flavor nearing the medium-full line. The burn was dead straight throughout the experience, with nary a touchup required. Ash was firm and held over an inch throughout.

note_sources.text: A medium to full bodied cigar that is complex and flavorful, Allegiance offers the smoker notes of spice, nut, sweetness and a slight hint of black coffee.

E.P. Carrillo Allegiance is the fourth installment in the world famous Perez-Carrrillo lineup, following La Historia , Encore , and Pledge . Some would say this series is one of the most successful ever, as two have earned cigar of the year and one was a close runner-up. That being said, Allegiance had to have a lot to bring to the table. What is interesting about this cigar, however, is that unlike the first 3, Allegiance is made hundreds of miles away from Carrillo’s own Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic. In fact, Allegiance isn’t even made by one of Carrillo’s own factories! You read that right, this stick is actually hand-built in Esteli, Nicaragua at Tabacalera de Oliva! As for the blend, we have Nicaraguan binders and fillers and, of course, an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper leaf (Would you expect anything less from E.P. Carrillo?). The first run consisted of 150,000 cigars, but more may be rolled depending on demand. All things considered; it goes without saying that Allegiance was destined for big things. Soon after its release, it earned multiple 95 ratings from Cigar Aficionado , and the Allegiance Confidant ranked #5 in 2023 , proving it has what it takes to stand among the finest Perez-Carrillo cigars. Bearing the all-too-familiar Perez-Carrillo Series attire, Allegiance stands out from the crowd with bright green and gold colors. The green ribbon around the foot denotes the brand, and the overall presentation is impeccably gorgeous. Looks aren’t where it ends, though. Each and every stick is made to exact specifications, undergoing rigorous quality inspections throughout the production process. This stick performs as well as any other cigar with E.P. Carrillo’s name on it, offering an easy, productive draw and copious clouds of thick, white smoke. This cigar opens up with a burst of spicy Nicaraguan pepper , quickly settling down to an array of cedar, dark chocolate, and cinnamon . The entire flavor profile is built around a rock-solid core of earthy raw tobacco goodness. The finish is long, smooth, and powerful, yet all-in-all Allegiance finishes as a solid medium-full-bodied cigar . While there is nothing particularly fancy about the blend itself, Allegiance, like its other Perez-Carrillo counterparts, is aimed at a more experienced crowd. Considered an ultra-premium offering, this blend is medium-full-bodied, complex and satisfying. It pairs well with scotch, bourbon, or cognac, and is a great way to settle down after dinner. It doesn’t take a rocket scientist to know that this cigar is destined for greatness. Following in some of the biggest footsteps in cigar history, it is already on the right path. Whether you are a long-time fan of E.P. Carrillo cigars or just want to see what a “Cigar of the Year” caliber cigar tastes like, you will never go wrong with Allegiance by E.P. Carrillo.

Some cigars make an impression from the very first draw. Others reveal their true character over time. The E.P. Carrillo Deep Blue Limited Edition was created to do exactly that. Inspired by the unexplored depths of the ocean and the mythology of Hades, where the greatest mysteries lie beneath the surface, Deep Blue reflects Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's long-time philosophy that the finest cigars are those that continue to evolve throughout the entire smoking experience. Every draw invites you to go a little deeper, rewarding patience with new layers of flavor and complexity. Handcrafted at the renowned Casa Carrillo factory in the Dominican Republic, this limited-edition release features a beautiful Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper over a Honduran binder and carefully selected Nicaraguan long-fillers. The blend was meticulously developed to progress naturally, allowing each tobacco to contribute its own character as the cigar unfolds. Rather than delivering its full strength immediately, Deep Blue builds with remarkable balance, offering a refined medium-plus profile that grows richer and more expressive from beginning to end. Construction is flawless, reinforcing E.P. Carrillo's reputation for uncompromising quality and exceptional craftsmanship. The experience opens with a smooth sweetness accented by delicate floral notes before richer flavors of earth, cedar, leather, and baking spice gradually emerge. As the cigar develops, the body deepens and the spice becomes more pronounced, while the natural sweetness of the Jalapa wrapper continues to provide balance. Every transition feels deliberate, creating a dynamic smoking experience that rewards those who enjoy complexity that unfolds rather than overwhelms. Produced in just 2,500 individually numbered boxes of 20 cigars , the E.P. Carrillo Deep Blue Limited Edition is a rare expression of Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's mastery of balance, progression, and craftsmanship. Rich without excess, powerful without aggression, and endlessly engaging, Deep Blue is a cigar that reminds us the greatest discoveries are often found by those willing to venture a little deeper.

Notes of gin botanicals and some brown sugar are the main flavors at this point, with some tanginess on the back of the palate. note_sources.text: A 96-rated Nicaraguan Puro by Cigar Aficionado from one of the most respected Dominican cigar companies in the business, E.P. Carrillo Encore will have you cheering for a second as soon as you finish your first. Yes, all references to a musical encore in both this description and the cigar's frontmark are intentional. What, you didn't know that years ago a young Ernesto Perez-Carrillo was hoping to be a famous jazz drummer before coming back to his roots as a fourth-generation cigar-maker? Well, now you do. Treating tobacco blending as much an art as a science, Carrillo sourced a wide variety of fine Nicaraguan longleaf aged in tercios, meaning tied into bundles within royal palm leaves, resulting in a smooth yet powerful smoke you'll want to revisit again and again. On occasion, the look and feel of a cigar speaks directly to the performance that the lucky smoker is about to experience. Heavily laden with succulent tobacco the box-pressed barrel of an E.P. Carrillo Encore wears its cream-colored foot ribbon and dual copper and gold bands with confidence, reflective of its creator's skill as developed through years of rigorous practice and training. The toothy, oily wrapper contains the aroma of rich tobacco and crisp fresh hay, thrilling the nose while the tongue detects a flourish of pepper during the cold draw test. Beginning dry and with deep notes of turned earth and charred oak when first lit, the cigar's flavor soon brightens and expands to include black tea and sweet cream . Building slowly into full-bodied flavor, the strength remains a firm medium even as a crescendo of leather, citrus, and caramel washes over the palate. Only a virtuoso of tobacco such as Ernesto Perez-Carrillo could create a monumental smoke like the E.P. Carrillo Encore. These premium cigars are a ticket to taste, relaxation, and pure enjoyment so pour yourself a favorite beverage, put on some swinging tunes, and sit back. Just don't be surprised when you light up another.

E.P. Carrillo is one of the most dominant names in the world of premium cigars, holding a near-permanent spot on “Best Of” lists and remaining among the most sought-after brands in any humidor. So, it comes as no surprise that whenever a new line is released under the E.P. Carrillo name, the entire cigar industry seems to pause and take notice. That was exactly the case with the launch of E.P. Carrillo Endure , which immediately drew attention as a blend destined for greatness. Produced at the Casa Carrillo factory in the Dominican Republic, Endure begins with a filler and binder blend of all-Nicaraguan premium tobaccos. The real standout, however, is the wrapper—an authentic African Cameroon leaf cultivated by the renowned Meerapfel family. Since Ernesto Perez-Carrillo rarely works with Cameroon wrappers, this release is nothing short of a big deal. Unsurprisingly, Endure earned multiple 91 ratings from Cigar Aficionado right out of the gate. Presented in striking orange-branded boxes, these box-pressed masterpieces wear three orange-and-gold bands along with a tissue wrap. The bold E.P. Carrillo logo gleams proudly across the main band, reminding aficionados that when Ernesto puts his name on a cigar, uncompromising quality is guaranteed. Consistency is a hallmark here—each vitola offers effortless draws and produces dense, aromatic clouds of smoke. Flavors begin with cedar and earthy raw tobacco , gradually unfolding into layers of cream, fresh bread, and black pepper , with a subtle sweetness lingering on the finish . Medium-to-full-bodied, Endure is as flavorful as it is balanced, a true testament to its prestigious name. Designed for seasoned enthusiasts, Endure embodies the qualities true connoisseurs look for: depth, complexity, balance, and a strength level that is smooth yet satisfying. It pairs beautifully with bourbon, scotch, or a medium-bodied beer, making it an excellent choice for celebratory occasions. Fans of other renowned Perez-Carrillo blends such as La Historia or Encore will no doubt find Endure to be equally compelling. Genuine Cameroon over Nicaraguan tobaccos, crafted under the watchful eye of one of the greatest figures in modern cigar making—this is the essence of E.P. Carrillo Endure. Experience the future of ultra-premium cigars today.

Carrillo Essence Connecticut continues that philosophy as the fourth addition to the acclaimed Essence Series, joining the Maduro, Sumatra, and Honduras blends with a profile designed to be smooth, balanced, and endlessly enjoyable. Crafted at the renowned Agroindustrias DIADEMA factory in Honduras, only the second Essence blend produced outside of Casa Carrillo, this cigar combines Honduran and Dominican fillers with a Honduran Criollo 98 binder and a silky Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. The recipe may be straightforward, but the smoking experience is anything but ordinary. The presentation is every bit as refined as the blend itself. A pale golden Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with a gentle sheen gives the cigar an elegant appearance, perfectly complemented by the Essence Series' modern black, gold, and red bands. Construction is impeccable, producing a razor-sharp burn, a firm light-gray ash, and thick clouds of smooth, aromatic smoke. Layers of toasted almond and cedar soon emerge, while a subtle sweetness and classic tobacco character linger in the background. The finish is clean, balanced, and satisfying, settling comfortably at a medium body without ever becoming heavy. Made for smokers who appreciate nuance and craftsmanship, the Essence Connecticut is approachable enough for newer enthusiasts yet refined enough to earn a place in any seasoned aficionado's rotation. Its smooth profile pairs beautifully with a morning coffee, a light bourbon, or a crisp lager, making it one of the most versatile cigars in the Essence lineup. If you seek massive amounts of sweet flavor from huge cigars, let us introduce you to the immensely tasty E.P. Carrillo Inch Maduro. So, it should be obvious already that these stogies are large, but don’t go thinking of them as a one-trick Clydesdale-sized pony. Oh no, because creator Ernesto Perez-Carrillo has earned his status as one of the biggest names in the tobacco business by churning out hit cigars one after the other, and the Inch Maduro is yet another top-rated colossus. Built using a vast wealth of premium longleaf filler from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic, these hefty vitolas are transformed into enormous triumphs with a flawlessly fermented Broadleaf Maduro wrapper of exceptional quality. Don’t forget to stretch before lifting a heavy E.P. Carrillo Inch Maduro from your humidor and make sure your cutter and lighter are up to the task of granting access to the generous flavors stored at the core. Despite the over-abundance of tobacco skillfully rolled into the barrel, you’ll find a rich draw and sultry flavors within moments of getting the broad foot fully smoldering. The palate will first detect semi-sweet dark chocolate coating thick layers of earth and oak, the cigar’s strength slowly building towards a creamy medium-full. With the latter half of the smoke a slow-burning tour, expect plenty of black coffee spiked with amaretto, some bursts of nutmeg and allspice, and a dollop of salted caramel. The sheer amount of enjoyment to be found in just one E.P. Carrillo Inch Maduro, makes the fact that they come in gargantuan yet affordable cabinets of 24 makes them even more appealing, don’t you think? You’ll need to dedicate plenty of time for the full experience, so make sure you have something smaller but equally as delicious on hand, maybe some cigarillos from Gran Habano or a tin of Davidoff Primeros Maduro, for when a short smoke break is all you’ve got. 70 Nat: 7 X 70 Taste – Medium Full-Flavored Born big to smoke bigger, the INCH Natural is the ultimate choice for aficionados who appreciate a substantial ring gauge. The INCH Natural delights the palate with its full-bodied flavor profile. Smokers will savor the robust spice, earthy undertones, and woody notes that dominate each puff. As you progress through the smoke, a subtle nutty flavor emerges on the back end, adding an intriguing layer of complexity to the overall experience.

The origin of a cigar's name can sometimes be an enigma, perhaps wrapped in history or obscurity, or even a private joke, but not so with the E.P. Carillo Inch Natural. It starts with identifying the creator as none other than the esteemed Ernesto Perez-Carillo, a man who every day honors his four generations of tobacco history but creating some of the world's best handmade smokes. Next, of course, is Inch, easily explained once you realize that the broad ring gauge of each vitola in the line measures close to an inch. Finally, the Natural Ecuadorian wrapper that completes the cigar adds a smooth, medium-strength character to the bold Dominican and Nicaraguan tobacco within. Appropriately heavy in hand, you'll marvel at the skill involved in creating such an imposing stogie, the oily barrel sleek and flawless. The well-rolled filler tobacco within gives only slightly to pressure, revealing no soft spots and promising a pleasing draw that is confirmed during a cold draw test. The soft wood and spice detected on the tongue erupt into crisp cedar and fiery black pepper as soon as the E.P. Carillo Inch Natural is lit, thick clouds of smoke pouring forth to fill the room with a floral aroma. Mellowing slightly after the initial rush, the profile is a medley of espresso, tanned leather, earthy-sweet vanilla, warm buttered biscuit, and a touch of citrus peel. Carillo Inch Natural, too. Maybe splitting a box will be the way to go, that way, you could also buy some El Rey Del Mundo Oscuro and Diesel Esteli Puros to really fill your cache. Each puff provides a symphony of flavors, making it a joy to smoke and a must-have addition to any cigar aficionado’s collection. Its robust and intricate flavor profile ensures that it will quickly become a staple in your regular rotation. Embrace the complexity and richness of the INCH Nicaragua , a cigar that stands out not only for its impressive big ring gauge but also for its unparalleled flavor and quality. Elevate your smoking experience with the full-flavored excellence of the INCH Nicaragua, and discover why it is a quintessential choice for discerning smokers.

Ernesto Perez-Carrillo is best known for his industry-dominating Dominican cigars, but has in recent years started experimenting with Nicaraguan tobaccos, and with great success. One such successful achievement is Inch Nicaragua, the third regular production installment to the well-known, larger-than-life Inch series, following Inch Natural and Inch Maduro . For this blend, Carrillo decided to collaborate with one of the best-known names in all of Nicaraguan tobacco: The Plasencia Family. Made in the Plasencia factory in Nicaragua, also known as El Cathedral, Inch Nicaragua is a true Nicaraguan puro, meaning it is entirely made of Nicaraguan tobacco—wrapper, filler, and binder. The filler blend contains aged tobacco from Plasencia’s farms in Condega and Esteli, and the wrapper is a golden brown shade-grown leaf from Jalapa. The result is a spicy, well-rounded cigar set to satisfy the cravings of even the most enthusiastic fan of Nicaraguan cigars . Such a bold cigar should include bold packaging, and this is certainly the case with Inch Nicaragua. The label is simple and loud, yet refined and premium in appearance, a great way to compliment the cigar beneath the band. Construction on each and every stout vitola is immaculate, lending to a soft, productive draw and a tight white ash. The flavor journey, like that of most Nicaraguan puros, starts off spicy and intense. This soon settles to an earthy, chocolaty array of flavor that holds everything together, speckled along the way with blasts of cedar and nuts. A creamy texture overtakes the blend about halfway through, and the finish is dry, clean, and peppery. For an all-Nicaraguan cigar, this blend certainly presents a very interesting and complex flavor profile. Inch Nicaragua finishes on the heavy side, just about a notch below full-bodied. This cigar is by no means a beginners’ cigar by definition, but it sure makes a great way to get into heavier cigars for someone with a bit of experience. It also presents a gateway to get into the shorter, fatter cigars that have become so popular in recent years. Inch Nicaragua pairs well with coffee or full-bodied beer and is appropriate for just about any time of the day. Fans of such fat sticks as Nub Habano or Cain F Nub will definitely be impressed by the stature and flavor profile this cigar has to offer. E.P. Carrillo is one of the best in the business, so you know that any cigar bearing his name is going to be a hit. That being said, what are you waiting for. The time is now to experience one of the hottest new cigars to come out of Nicaragua with E.P. Carrillo Inch Nicaragua. Shop more E.P. Carrillo Cigars:

The first few puffs of the La Historia are a bit mixed together. The biggest flavor is a smokiness, maybe a burning cherry wood, with a hefty mouthfeel lingering well onto the next draw. The finish does, however, leave a sweetness on the palate, similar to a cherry-like flavor that mixes well with the smoke. The retro-hale provides a nice increase of flavors as well, with a somewhat harsh white pepper, spices, and a very deep wood flavor that I can’t quite identify. The construction is fair so far, providing a good draw, but low smoke output. The ash holds on extremely well, never falling off till I tapped it around the halfway point. The cigar is a solid full body throughout the first third, finishing off with mostly “meaty” flavors, along with dark cherry, a little spice, and the smoked wood. Down to the nub, the La Historia never really changes. Remaining full body and medium-full strength, the lasting impact of flavors are smoked wood, sweet cherry, dark chocolate, a spice infusion, and a decent pepper kick on the retro-hale. The burn is great, lasting a good 1.5 – 2 hours, depending on the smoker, along with a very tight and consistent ash.

In 2010, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr., the architect behind the success of the modern La Gloria Cubana, introduced the E.P. Carrillo Core Line, and announced that a Connecticut cigar was to follow shortly. What Ernesto didn't tell the world was that he was going to try to reinvent the perception of Connecticut shade wrappers. The man that redefined Maduro named his newest line NWC, New Wave Connecticut. The result was a Dominican-made cigar that features an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan fillers offered in five sizes: Briliantes (5" x 50), Stellas (5 1/8" x 42), Divinos (6" x 52), El Decano (6" x 60) and Gran Via (7" x 49). The E.P. Carrillo New Wave Connecticut is not your typical Connecticut. While it's still medium in strength, the body and flavor are anything but strong. Even though most Connecticut's offer some form of pepper, the NWC features a significantly more developed flavor that shows complexities of cedar, leather, earth and cocoa. There's a decent amount of creaminess that begins to remind you that this is still very much Connecticut. While there is no individual flavor that would be considered mystical, it's the overall flavor that is so unique as far as Connecticuts go. Simply put, there is no Connecticut offered on the market that features as much flavor and complexity as the E.P. Carrillo NWC. This is a perfect cigar for those just getting started and great for those experienced smokers who have overlooked Connecticut due to its normal limitations. Check out other E.P. note_sources.text: This full-bodied masterpiece is crafted with the finest tobaccos, delivering a rich and complex flavor profile that has captivated cigar enthusiasts worldwide. 1 Cigar of the Year – Cigar Aficionado rated 98 Prequel: Tobacco Business Best Dominican Cigar of 2021 Prequel: Cigar Journal Best Dominican Cigar of 2021 Prequel: Cigar Dojo Cigar of the Year 2020 Sojourn: Rated 91 by Cigar Aficionado Magazine Apogee: Rated 93 by Cigar Aficionado Magazine Taste – Full-Flavored Our boldest expression in a cigar that is full of rich complex flavors. Expect a powerhouse of flavors with the Pledge . From the first draw, you’ll experience noticeable spice and robust wood notes, balanced by a hint of sweetness.

E.P. Carrillo Pledge is one of the most anticipated and coveted releases in the history of the brand. The third installment in the acclaimed Perez-Carrillo series—following La Historia and Encore —Pledge is widely regarded as the crowning achievement of Ernesto Perez-Carrillo, often called “The Godfather of Boutique Cigars.” Hand-rolled exclusively by the expert torcedors at Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic, Pledge features a meticulously crafted blend of ultra-premium tobaccos from three countries: Nicaraguan filler, an Ecuadorian binder, and a rich, dark Connecticut Habano wrapper grown in the U.S.A. Its predecessors set a high bar—La Historia earned a 95 rating and ranked No. 2 in 2014, while Encore reached a 96 rating and topped the charts in 2018. Pledge not only met those expectations in 2020, but surpassed them, achieving a historic 98 rating and claiming the No. 1 spot in the year’s top 25. This is a cigar collectors and aficionados alike are eager to experience. Presented in classic Perez-Carrillo style, Pledge comes in lacquered cedar boxes adorned with luxurious blue and gold artwork and finished with an elegant ribbon around each cigar’s foot. The construction is flawless: an effortless draw produces dense, billowing smoke, a crisp, even burn, and firm, gray ash. The box-press design adds a refined feel in the hand and a comfortable draw in the mouth. On the palate, Pledge opens with bold black pepper and lively Nicaraguan spice, gradually giving way to a smooth blend of earthy tobacco, toasted nuts, and rich espresso. Hints of cinnamon, cocoa, and subtle bread notes weave throughout, while the retrohale delivers a distinctly sweet finish. Medium-full-bodied, Pledge maintains perfect balance from start to finish. Pledge, like all cigars in the Perez-Carrillo series, is designed for experienced connoisseurs. Its sophisticated and multi-layered profile rewards those with a refined palate. Ideal for pairing with red wine, cognac, or bold coffee, it elevates any special occasion. While standing proudly alongside La Historia and Encore, Pledge also rivals other ultra-premium cigars such as Padron 1964 and Diamond Crown Maximus . With each release, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo continues to showcase his unparalleled blending skill and rich heritage. Highly sought-after and limited in availability, Pledge is a must-have for any serious cigar enthusiast eager to experience one of the finest cigars of our era.

The first few puffs bring a lighter body with medium strength; the draw is a little tight but I get a nice white pepper on the retrohale. Right off the bat, there is a zesty spice, almost like wasabi through the nostrils. This cigar is loaded with cabinet spices and there is a dash of nutmeg on the finish. It has some spice to it but is not necessarily full-bodied at this point, which is refreshing. Smooth smoke is pouring out on each puff and I am impressed by how silky and refined this cigar starts. The ash is dark grey and almost Cubanesque in appearance (I’m not saying the cigar tastes Cuban, but I feel like you, the reader, could file this away for future consideration), usually a sign of rich minerals in the soil. There is a chai tea flavor as the cigar develops; it’s this sweet-ish spice that reminds me of warm tea. I have had to do a couple of touchups and the draw is just a tad under what I would consider to be ideal. The burn is slightly wonky, but the peppery, cabinet spice flavor still appears prominently. I like that this cigar is very spice-forward and has a solid bit of strength, yet still maintains a near-medium body and some nuance and refinement. At this point, I’d still consider this a cigar that you could smoke in the morning because it doesn’t have that full-bodied punch that you find yourself seeking as the day winds down. The draw has really loosened moving past the halfway mark. I initially got a somewhat papery flavor with a tartness on the tongue but that quickly dissipates. A roasted nut flavor with some spice starts to move to the forefront; it kind of reminds me of those cinnamon-roasted almonds that you find at a fair. I have had to relight a couple of times—construction has been less than perfect throughout but hasn’t taken away from the performance much. As I approach the band, there is a bit more bitterness; there is kind of a burnt toast quality to the final bit of this cigar. Green chili flavors rush through the retrohale, true to the spicy quality that has been prevalent throughout the cigar. It has a pretty earthy base on the palate and hasn’t had too many noticeable changes from start to finish.

note_sources.text: Second Generation Cigar Makers, Alec and Bradley Rubin announced today that they will be expanding distribution of their inaugural release: Alec & Bradley Blind Faith at the Tobacco Plus Expo (TPE) in Las Vegas, NV- January 29-31. Under the tutelage of their father, Alec Bradley Cigar Co. founder Alan Rubin, the brothers began planning their own brand in 2017. Since they were both untested in the cigar business, they decided to name their cigar Blind Faith. Blind Faith was released to appointed merchants during the International Premium Cigar & Pipe Retailers Association (IPCPR) in 2018. “Alec & Bradley Cigars has grown leaps and bounds since our first introduction,” said Bradley Rubin. “Since the early success of Blind Faith, we had the opportunity to team up with the legendary Ernie Perez-Carrillo for our second release, Gatekeeper. As well, Alec and I are about to release Uru Doshi with Cigar Dojo. Alec and I both feel like we have gained the trust of tobacconists and enthusiasts. We asked for more capacity at Raices Cubanas to increase production of Blind Faith and we got it. Now we have the ability to get Blind Faith in the hands of more cigar lovers.” The Blind Faith blend features a wrapper from Alec Bradley’s proprietary farm in Trojes, Honduras. Three different fillers from Esteli are held together by a double binder combination from Honduras and Nicaragua. Unlike the Alec Bradley tradition of blending for flavor first and strength levels later- Alec and Bradley focused on taking bolder tobaccos and blending them for strength with great flavor and balance. “Bradley and I are very excited to expand the availability of Blind Faith,” said Alec Rubin. “This is the first time Alec & Bradley and Alec Bradley will be exhibiting at TPE; we thought that the show was a great opportunity to share this very special moment in our careers.” Blind Faith Formats and Prices: 5 x 52 Ring, Robusto | MSRP: $8.95 6 x 52 Ring, Toro | MSRP: $10.00 6 x 60 Ring, Gordo | MSRP: $10.95 Packaging: 20-count boxes Shipping: Global sales will begin on January 29

Joya de Nicaragua Antano 1970 is a legend of a cigar. Originally born in the mid-1960s, Joya de Nicaragua was produced in Nicaragua's first cigar factory. As the years went by, however, Communist rule, war, and extreme poverty tore apart the country, including that old factory. Thankfully, though, times are better now, and with Nicaragua at the forefront of the cigar industry, the tobacco business is a booming one in the tiny Central American hot spot. Joya de Nicaragua made a comeback several years ago, this time under the brand of Antano 1970, which literally means "Yesteryear 1970" or "Back Then 1970," a fitting title paying homage to the brand's humble roots and glory days. The brand now resides under the Drew Estate umbrella, so it's definitely in good hands. Known by many as the "Original Nicaraguan Puro," Antano 1970, offers a mind-numbing blend of unusually stout Nicaraguan ligero tobaccos. That inner package is then finished with a thick, dark Nicaraguan Habano Colorado wrapper leaf. The end result is what has been dubbed the world's strongest cigar. See all Joya De Nicaragua cigars . Dark brown with deep red hues, the Nicaraguan Habano Colorado wrapper drips with natural oils. Joya de Nicaragua Antano 1970, is rugged in appearance, yet expertly crafted and nearly seamless on the roll. A firm, yet productive draw offers thick ribbons of blue smoke, heavily coating the palate like honey. Sweet black cherry, faint cedar, and a dash of Nicaraguan pepper are the main notes, soon followed by long dashes of cocoa and subtle hints of coffee. The finish is sweet and floral; no doubt a signature of Antano's rich ligero fillers. The room note from Antano 1970 is also surprisingly sweet, making this stick a potential conversation starter at the cigar lounge. Full-bodied, smooth, and brilliantly blended, Antano 1970 is most definitely a gem of a cigar. When people talk about Antano 1970 being the world's strongest cigar, they really aren't kidding. It may not slap your palate as you smoke it, but don't be fooled by its unreal smoothness and decadent flavor, as Antano 1970 will sneak up on even the most seasoned connoisseurs if smoked on an empty stomach. Antano pairs well with port wine, coffee, or cognac and should only be enjoyed by those with experience regarding full-flavored sticks. If you are daring enough to try an Antano 1970, you may also want to look into its two ultra-full-bodied counterparts: Antano 1970 Dark Corojo and Antano 1970 Gran Reserva . Whether you call it "Yesteryear's Cigar," "The World's Strongest Stogie," or simply "Joya," Joya de Nicaragua Antano 1970, is still regarded as one of the great cigars of our time and will doubtless be renowned for years to come. Joya de Nicaragua Antano Dark Corojo is the follow-up cigar to the world-famous Antano 1970 , which is considered by many to be the world's strongest cigar. Well, maybe it was the strongest, until Antano Dark Corojo came along. Released a full decade after the Antano 1970 , Antano Dark Corojo took what connoisseurs loved about the 1970 and "kicked it up a notch," so to speak. Long considered to be a more elegant, aficionado-style cigar, Antano Dark Corojo takes spice, flavor, and overall strength to entirely new levels. Like all Joya de Nicaragua cigars, Antano Dark Corojo is made in Nicaragua and is marketed under the Drew Estate umbrella of brands. The incredible recipe for this top shelf masterpiece consists of Nicaraguan filler tobaccos from all 3 of Nicaragua's top growing regions, a spicy Nicaraguan binder, and a dark Nicaraguan Corojo Oscuro wrapper leaf. Along with an updated recipe, a new level of strength and complexity, and luxurious black packaging, Antano Dark Corojo is offered in a variety of sizes, each decided upon based on the preferences of experienced connoisseurs. See all Joya De Nicaragua cigars. Antano Dark Corojo's 3-year-aged, dark brown, nearly black wrapper leaf oozes with glistening oils. The construction, like its predecessor, is rugged, yet elegant and seamless. An amazing roll produces a slow, cool burn and a solid, yet plentiful draw, blasting the palate with a rush of cedar and earth mingled with spicy Nicaraguan white pepper. Cocoa, black cherry, cinnamon, and leather round out the flavor profile, followed by a subtle floral burst on the finish. Overall, Antano Dark Corojo is rich, powerful, and unusually smooth. Without a doubt, it's over-the-top on the fullness scale. Obviously Antano Dark Corojo isn't a beginners' cigar. Heck, it isn't even a cigar for a seasoned enthusiast. But then again, it was never meant to be. The good people at Joya Cigars specifically intended Antano Dark Corojo to be for experienced connoisseurs. In addition, even those experienced connoisseurs should never smoke Antano Dark Corojo on an empty stomach. In fact, it makes a great finishing touch to a steak dinner, especially paired with espresso or port wine. If you enjoyed the original Antano 1970 , or are just a fan of extremely full-bodied cigars in general, there's no reason not to try this amazing offering from Joya Cigars. The "Yesteryear Cigar" has been revived, updated, and overhauled. Now it's better than ever. Don't take our word for it, though. Try a Joya de Nicaragua Antano Dark Corojo today and taste for yourself the true heritage of Nicaraguan cigars. Over the past decade, Joya de Nicaragua has celebrated several anniversaries with cigars that have absolutely rocked the industry, so it is without question that when work started on Joya de Nicaragua Cinco de Cinco, the company’s 55 th anniversary cigar, the bar was set unimaginably high. For this project, the folks at Joya de Nicaragua started by having private blending sessions with both consumers and industry personnel, and they took the information they gathered at said events and decided on what the ideal recipe would be. They eventually settled on what they would call “the perfect scoring recipe,” which includes high-grade Nicaraguan filler and binder leaves beneath an ultra-vintage Mexican San Andres wrapper. Part of Joya de Nicaragua’s top offerings known as Obras Maestras, or “Masterpieces,” Cinco de Cinco made its debut with flying colors, earning a pair of stout 92 ratings in Cigar Aficionado and, more importantly, taking the entire cigar world by storm. Made by the incredibly skilled artisans at Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua, the ultra-premium vitolas are housed in shiny green and white boxes, each stick clothed with a beautiful green, white, and gold band. The box-pressed construction is nothing short of impeccable, with each and every easy puff yielding billowing clouds of dense, white smoke. As can be expected, the experience starts off with a blast of spicy Nicaraguan pepper, soon to be followed by rich cedar and sweet cinnamon. The earthy background is complemented by robust notes of dark chocolate and cocoa, along with a creamy undertone of floral sweetness. This sweetness is particularly noticeable on the retrohale, doubtless an allusion to the world-famous Antano 1970 that put the company on the map in the first place. The finish is smooth, strong, and spicy, and overall Cinco de Cinco settles at the high end of medium-full-bodied. The “Masterpiece” cigars from JDN are intended for a very experienced audience, so it is inevitably understood that Cinco de Cinco is no beginners’ cigar. Rich, complex, and highly refined, this cigar is meant for only the most discerning palates. It pairs well with coffee, port wine, or dark rum and is best enjoyed slowly, with plenty of time to savor each and every puff. If you have tried the other “Masterpiece” offerings from JDN, including Numero Uno , Cuatro Cinco , and Cinco Decadas , it is only right to give Cinco de Cinco a shot, and decide for yourself if it compares well to its top-shelf counterparts. We don’t doubt you’ll be impressed, but please, don’t take our word for it. Try a Joya de Nicaragua Cinco de Cinco and celebrate the long legacy of one of the most legendary cigar brands on the planet.

Joya de Nicaragua and Drew Estate have been doing big things in the world of cigars recently, and many would argue that Joya de Nicaragua Numero Uno is the crowning achievement. The story behind this blend is that long before it became a commercially available cigar for purchase, it was a blend handed out as a diplomatic gift by Nicaraguan ambassadors and government officials to visiting dignitaries. It is also said that the blend was originally destined to be a special handout at Drew Estate events across the US. Nevertheless, Numero Uno is thankfully here for all of us to enjoy, and what a treat it is! Produced by individual pairs of cigar rollers at Fabrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua, this blend is part of Joya de Nicaragua's Obras Maestras series, translated simply as "Masterpieces," the brand's most limited and sought-after products. On the surface, Numero Uno seems to be a simple blend, using Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf. In reality, however, this cigar is a high-end performer and offers some of the most luxurious flavor available on today's market. Don't believe us? We can let the 95 rating in Cigar Aficionado do the talking, along with the high placing Numero Uno earned on the Top 25 list for 2020.

The Story
The Espinosa Habano is the cigar that started it all, the first to be blended by Espinosa Cigars after starting its own company. A traditional Habano blend that is anything but traditional, this complex offering is medium bodied, balanced, and full of spice, cocoa, and cedar notes. It’s not just a cigar, A traditional Habano blend that is anything but traditional, this complex offering is medium bodied, balanced, and full of spice, cocoa, and cedar notes.

The re-blended Espinosa Habano is a powerhouse cigar from a man unafraid to improve upon past success. The original Habano released by Erik Espinosa's La Zona factory, was a certified hit, raking in a couple of solid 90 ratings and delighting fans of medium to full smokes worldwide. This might be enough for your average cigar manufacturer, but Espinosa knew he could do more with what was basically one of his core brands. To this end, choice Nicaraguan tobaccos were sourced to create a complex and potent filler and binder combination that evolved into a full-bodied masterpiece with the addition of a meaty Ecuadorian Habano wrapper of exquisite quality. (Shop more Habano wrapper cigars ) A new band design, resplendent with blue and gold, decorates the retooled Espinosa Habano in elegant counterpoint to the dark, leathery, and oily wrapper. Wafting herbal and woody aromas, the unlit vitola displays excellent construction technique and feels substantial beneath the fingers. Clipped and aflame, the slowly smoldering barrel of the cigar releases cedar, alfalfa, cashew, and black pepper flavors in dense waves of creamy smoke. Transitioning towards the second half, a succulent floral scent in the air accompanies deep pockets of coffee, spice, and leather on the tongue. There's even a touch of sweetness that cuts through the strength to keep you reaching for the nub. As amazing of a feat as it was for Espinosa to improve on his original Habano, the fact that the price of this new cigar remains in line with the old is just as awe-inspiring. Fans of the original should not despair because the new Espinosa Habano remains faithful to the spirit of the past while forging a path to the hearts and minds of those aficionados not yet lucky enough to have discovered the brand. Either way, it is time to get to smoking!

The Story
This is definitely not your grandfather’s candela! The Espinosa Cigars Wasabi is a medium-plus flavored cigar with earthy sweetness and spice throughout. The Wasabi’s unique smoking experience will make you reconsider candela cigars forever.     THE VITOLAROBUSTO BP 5×52     Corona 5×42      Lancero  7½×38 The Espinosa Cigars Wasabi is a medium-plus flavored cigar with earthy sweetness and spice throughout.

As advertised, spicy flavors are delivered upon lighting. The notes are of raw peppercorn and burning brush and are more apparent as sensations across the tongue, rather than a burning spice through the nostrils. But the spices are quick to migrate, becoming the zesty sensation aforementioned within the cigar’s first half-inch. There are dark spices (black pepper and cumin), joined by vegetation (grass and hay) and a subtle, tangy sweetness that enters the profile around the one-inch mark. The Habano cap is an appreciated touch that adds a bit of peanut saltiness on the tongue—one of the cigar’s most enjoyable attributes throughout the first third. Wasabi is essentially medium in its strength, body, and flavor—perhaps a touch under medium in the flavor department. The smoke carries a dry texture, only barely registering on the front of the tongue (sweetness), primarily activating the middle (bitterness) and a little on the sides (saltiness). Despite the cigar’s extremely easy pre-light draw, the smoking draw is on the firm side (a 7 or 8 out of 10, with 5 being dead medium). Luckily, this doesn’t have much of an effect on the smoke output, which is about medium. In the middle portion of the robusto there are aspects that hint at the cigar’s name, burning through the nostrils with a wasabi/mustard-like zing. The strength increases and Wasabi tops out around medium/full strength, medium flavor, and a body somewhere in between. In the final third, a touch-up was required, igniting rich cabinet spices of cardamom, allspice, and clove. As these flavors dwindle, the cigar signals its end.

note_sources.text: From the wrapper I smell yeasty bread, chocolate, and sweet whipped cream with the papery, woody aroma of roasting coffee beans. From the foot it’s more of the yeast bread and chocolate, with a slight twinge of spiciness. The cold draw is sort of a muddy, earthy version of the aroma from the foot. It’s got a light twang that, in keeping with the bready theme, reminds me of a bubbling sourdough starter. On the back of all that is a Manischewitz wine fruitiness. The slight hint of spiciness that I detected in the aroma of the unlit cigar turns into the real deal upon ignition. The smoke is chewy, big, round, spicy, and abundant. Initial flavors are driven by an earthiness that is like cowboy coffee—full-bodied and gritty, with oak riding shotgun on a beer run. The abundant yeasty flavors have turned into that of a Trappist red ale, and it is a spectacular flavor note that I can’t remember tasting in the original version. The burn line is great, the ash forms into tight little stacks, the result of perfect construction and even combustion. The earthiness and spiciness combine into freshly cracked black peppercorn, and a fruity cacao flavor that is balanced with creamy oak. The yeast-like note is now akin to a Belgian waffle, toasty and rich. The long cigar burns slowly, and after nearly 40 minutes it’s time to move into the second third. Strength has been in a pleasant medium range, with a medium/full body (this is a big plus for me, as I have felt a little “green” after smoking 601 Blue Labels on more than one occasion). Fruitiness and creaminess are picking up near the midpoint of the cigar, with the earthiness just hanging on the back of the tongue like the sediment from a cup of French-pressed coffee. Come to think of it, coffee is the best descriptor of how these flavors all come together. The wood, earth, fruit, and cream remind me of juicy Kenyan coffee with a hint of black pepper. The flavors detectable on the retrohale get particularly exciting past the midway point, and I get a hint of black walnut, maple candy, coffee ice cream. This cigar is exploding with flavor at this point, with strength ramping up to medium/full (thankfully no room spins though). A swirling of flavors abound, and as I near the end of the second third the black pepper note is backed by black berry jam sweetness, charred buttered toast and that dark cacao. This cigar is really staying interesting. After nearly an hour and forty minutes, heading into the final third, the Short Churchill is oaky, fruity, peppery, and delicious. The fruitiness reminds me of the prune flavor associated with perique pipe tobacco. The burn isn’t as pretty as the first half, as the ash gets ugly and flaky, but corrections haven’t been necessary. We are now in full speed, full strength, knockout mode. Juicy, sticky, sweet prunes, cacao, cream, pepper, and smokey charred coffee beans—the profile is superb. The nub is cool, the pepper tingles, and my heart is singing joyous praises to this cigar. Some pleasing earthiness arrives as I finish the cigar at just over 2 hours of smoke time.
note_sources.title: 601 Blue Label Maduro Short Churchill

note_sources.text: The toro starts off with a sharp black pepper blast, leaving mineral flavor through the finish. This only intensifies with added draws, being a good wakeup call to start the experience. However, the cigar begins to settle after a few minutes, pulling back on spice (though not necessarily on punchiness) with a good dose of fairly sweet Chocolate Fudge Pop-Tarts. There’s plenty of earth as well, though not in the overly dark and/or bitter way that maduros are sometimes associated with. It’s a sweet earth that doesn’t fatigue the palate, leading way to added notes of mocha and an occasional toffee-like finish. Unfortunately, the draw is not much better than the pre-light experience, causing a bit more effort than I’d like (about 8.5/10 in terms of resistance). This translates to the smoke output with medium-light (which is better than the draw would have you believe) puffs of smoke on each draw. There is a nice sweetness on the tongue from the cut tobaccos themselves, being clean on the palate and seeming to hit the tongue on the tip, back, and sides—it’s a somewhat mouthwatering texture
note_sources.title: Aganorsa Leaf Rare Leaf Reserve Maduro Toro

note_sources.text: Aganorsa is proud to announce an exclusive blend for their Aganorsa Select Program: Rare Leaf Reserve Maduro. Like the original Rare Leaf release, the maduro edition utilizes select lots on their best farms that produce exemplary leaf unique in both flavor and aroma. The result in this case is the boldest expression of Aganorsa’s signature flavor to date. A San Andres Maduro wrapper envelops a double binder and fillers consisting entirely of Aganorsa grown tobaccos from Jalapa and Estelí. “When we launched Rare Leaf in 2021, the idea was to provide our retail partners who make the commitment to our Aganorsa Select Program with a special blend they would have exclusivity on.” states Terence Reilly, who serves as Vice President of Sales and Marketing. “Due to the success of the original release and our Aganorsa Select retail partners’ enthusiasm for it, we are adding Rare Leaf Maduro, a truly powerful expression of Aganorsa tobacco and one I haven’t experienced before. This blend will make you sit up and pay attention while smoking or, as we say at Aganorsa, validating.” Rare Leaf Reserve will ship to participating Aganorsa Select Partners in May. Sizes will consist of a Robusto (5.25 x 52), Toro (6 x 54), and a box pressed Belicoso (6 x52). All three vitolas are packaged in boxes of 15 cigars. Suggested retail prices will range from $13.50 to $14.50.
