An ultra-premium of the highest caliber, the Diamond Crown Maximus cigar will rouse your senses and astound your expectations. As you may know, the venerable J.C. Newman Cigar Company, America's oldest family-owned manufacturer, has been steadily creating some of the world's finest smokes for over a century. To celebrate their 110th anniversary, they partnered with the renowned Fuente and Oliva families to create this flawless and full-bodied masterpiece of quality tobacco. Utilizing a secret Newman-crafted filler blend of Dominican longleaf, the master torcedors at Tabacalera A. Fuente y Cia finish each stick with an incomparable Ecuadoran Sungrown wrapper cultivated on Oliva's exclusive El Bajo farm. There's a confident sophistication carried by each stick unable to be hidden by the apparent ruggedness of the oily, veiny, and chocolate-hued Sumatra-seed leaf that sits beneath the cigar's heavily decorated band. Redolent with the aromas of expertly fermented tobacco and sweet alfalfa, the slight flex within the vitola's barrel promises the excellent draw proven by a cold test. The 93-rated Diamond Crown Maximus' true character presents itself as the first sips of cool, spice-laden smoke reach the lips, with white pepper, vanilla cream, and espresso coating the palate soon after. Honeyed biscuit and golden raisins offer syrupy counterpoint to the earthy leather, oak, sea salt, and black cherry, which form the flavor profiles foundation from head to foot. Treat yourself today to some Diamond Crown Maximus as they are well worth every hard-earned cent, and you deserve it. Indulge even further by hosting a friendly inter-collaborator competition between your stash of Maximus, a few Arturo Fuente Rosado Sungrown Magnum R, and a solid handful of Oliva V Maduro. Your enjoyment in determining the favorite will be epic.

Following the success of his Unholy Cocktail and Shorty, AJ Fernandez brings us the Diesel Unlimited cigar. The Diesel Unlimited cigar brings us long filler leaf from Nicaragua and Mexico while wrapping this bad boy, we have a Ecuadorian Habano. This Ecuadorian Habano Ligero is an awfully pretty shade reminiscent of a well-worn brown leather chair. The wrapper has a small bit of tooth that screams, "grip me." Like the Unholy Cocktail, the Unlimited gets one simple, effective, no frills band wrapped around the foot of the cigar. The Diesel Unlimited is a full flavored, full bodied cigar. The 1st third brings us intense pepper with a spicy sweet tang that I just can't place. This Unlimited is well packed and burns slow. I made the mistake of trying to smoke it fast and it became bitter. So I purged and slowed down to fix that problem. The 2nd third brings a pepper spice bomb that takes me by surprise. The ash is medium gray and holds well. The smoke production so far has been great and the draw is perfect with my punch. The last third down to the nub brings a peppercorn encrusted meaty steak flavor to the table. At this point, I'm just wondering if AJ Fernandez can do anything wrong. The Diesel Unlimited has superb construction, no burn issues, great flavors, excellent body, and an unbelievably low price, making this a great cigar for experienced smokers. Newer smokers should stick to the Unholy Cocktail for now. It has less body and won't leave you with "the spins."

Diesel Unlimited Maduro is a cigar for fans of big, bad, bold flavors that want just a bit more bang for their buck. Made in Nicaragua by none other than A.J. Fernandez and Company, Diesel Unlimited Maduro is not only one of the newer additions to the Diesel portfolio; it is quickly becoming one of the most popular. Honduran and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos rest inside a luscious San Andres binder. The package is finished with a rich, oily Pennsylvania Broadleaf Maduro wrapper leaf, making for one heck of a stout cigar. However, then, if you are a fan of Diesel cigars, you must already know a thing or two about stout cigars, eh? Gleaming with natural oils and masterfully rolled in typical Fernandez fashion, Diesel Unlimited Maduro practically begs to be smoked. An easy draw produces billowing clouds of thick, white smoke, opening with a burst of spicy pepper and raw tobacco. Sweet, chocolatey flavors collide with subtle savory notes throughout the smoke, along with hints of coffee and a leathery aroma. A sweet touch of cocoa on the finish seals the deal. Indubitably full-bodied from the get-go, Diesel Unlimited Maduro makes a serious impression. Obviously, Diesel Unlimited Maduro is not for the faint of heart. It is full-bodied, full-flavored, and ready to satisfy even the most hardcore strength, junkies. It pairs well with dark beer, coffee, or bourbon, and makes an excellent choice for after a hearty dinner. If you love the original Diesel blend, or some of the other great sticks from A.J. Fernandez, including New World or San Lotano Maduro , chances are you are going to go crazy about Diesel Unlimited Maduro. The best part is, Diesel Unlimited Maduro is just as affordable as it is delicious, so why not grab some today?

The Diesel brand was born in 2009, and since then has grown to be a household name among long-time cigar fanatics. Nearly a decade and a half later, the brand introduced what some would call their flagship, while others just call it a flippin’ good cigar: Diesel Vintage Series Maduro . Made at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua, this modern day classic is called Vintage for a reason: The rich Nicaraguan filler leaves are all aged no less than 5-8 years. Pair this stellar filler blend with a Nicaraguan Habano binder and a dark, oily San Andres wrapper leaf from Mexico, and you have the blend that would become one of the finest ever to be called a Diesel, and one that scored a rock-solid 91 in Cigar Aficionado magazine . Gray and gold boxes, gold accented bands, fancy script logos on every cigar, it all screams “luxury.” And that is exactly what this one is! While Diesel has been known for years to be big, bold, and rough around the edges, so to speak, this one shows the brand’s finer side, aligning more with AJ Fernandez’s typical style. An easy draw produces thick smoke with each puff, and the opening flavors are white pepper and rich coffee. An earthy core holds everything together, and heavy notes of cocoa, black cherry, and spice round out this classic maduro flavor profile . Spicy, heavy, and superbly balanced, Vintage Series Maduro finishes as a no-nonsense full-bodied cigar. Though it’s made for experienced enthusiasts, Vintage Series maduro is a great way for intermediate smokers to get into stronger blends. Full-bodied, this undeniably smooth blend pairs well with black coffee, dark beer, or your favorite dark rum. Fans of the original Diesel blend are sure to enjoy this one, as well as anyone who has enjoyed some of AJ’s famed maduro concoctions such as Enclave Broadleaf or San Lotano Maduro . Kick back, relax, and enjoy a whole new side of Diesel that we promise you’ve never seen, with Diesel Vintage Series Maduro.

Cream , Earth , Hazelnut , Spice Drink. A collaboration between Justin Andrews and AJ Fernandez, the Vintage Series provides exceptional quality, flavor, and value while staying true to the foundation that has and continues to set Diesel…

As a premium cigar brand, Diesel has come a long way since their introduction in 2009. Once more “under-the-radar,” the name is now recognized as one of the big ones in the business. That being said, it was no surprise when they introduced the original Diesel Vintage just a couple years ago, a luxury style cigar made with extensively-aged tobaccos through and through. Fast forward just a bit, and we have yet another variation: Diesel Vintage Series Natural. Made at the famed Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua, this top shelf offering uses filler leaves from Jalapa, Nicaragua, all aged no less than 5-7 years. The binder is from Esteli, and the wrapper is a golden brown Ecuadorian leaf. This recipe combines to make one of the tastiest cigars to ever sport the Diesel name. Oh, and did we mention the 91 rating in Cigar Aficionado ? Luxurious gold-accented boxes with individual slots lovingly cradle the expertly-constructed vitolas. Each stick wears a single white and gold band depicting a unique take on the standard Diesel insignia. Rolled to perform, this monster draws easily to give off massive plumes of dense, flavorful smoke. Earthy tobacco is the dominant flavor in this one, and it starts from the very first puff. Early on, it’s mingled with chocolate and nutty flavor , with just a hint of cedar in the background. Black pepper joins in after a bit, and the finish is crispy and spicy, with just a touch of sweetness . Full-bodied after all is said and done, this Diesel takes all the good things about the classic blends and fully refines them. This blend is obviously aimed at intermediate to experienced cigar enthusiasts. A seasoned palate is certainly desirable in order to be able to thoroughly appreciate this complex full-bodied beauty. It pairs well with your favorite scotch, dark rum, or full-bodied beer and is best enjoyed after a meal. Fans of the original Diesel or Diesel Whiskey Row are sure to enjoy this one, as it seems to keep the essential DNA of the flavor profile and expand on it. Once again, AJ Fernandez and company present a flavorful treat that won’t break the bank and satisfies every single time. Try a Diesel Vintage Series Natural today and experience it for yourself.

Since Diesel began collaborating with Rabbit Hole Distilling back in 2018, some of the most notable releases in the history of the brand have come into existence. One such release, the star of 2025, is Diesel Whiskey Row Founder’s Collection Raceking , the latest of the red-hot Founder’s Collection series that has been ongoing for some time now. This blend, made at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua like all Diesel sticks, consists of a Nicaraguan filler and binder blend combined with a beautiful Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. The key to the blend, surprisingly, is the binder leaf, a premium Nicaraguan varietal that has been extensively aged in barrels that previously held Rabbit Hole Raceking bourbon. This gentle infusion of bourbon flavor into the binder leaf gives the whole flavor profile a unique note that sets it in a class of its own. Packed in dressy brown and gold cedar boxes, each 6” x 52 Raceking cigar wears a solid gold main band in conjunction with a blue and orange foot band denoting the blend. The skilled team under the keen supervision of AJ Fernandez never skimps on construction, so rest assured that each and every cigar will perform phenomenally, offering thick, billowing clouds on every puff. Spicy white pepper is the opening note , no doubt a result of the hearty Nicaraguan fillers. The initial intensity smooths out into a medley of earth and cocoa, with hints of nuts and coffee along the way. The finish is sweet, with a touch of bourbon and cedar , and after all is said and done, Raceking finishes as a stout, full-bodied cigar. Though Diesel cigars have historically been appropriate for a vast array of cigar enthusiasts, the Founder’s collection is aimed at a more experienced group. Raceking, along with all the Founder’s Collection sticks, are made for the discriminating connoisseur that finds ultimate pleasure in a fine cigar. Full-bodied, intense, and flavorful, the sweet and spicy Raceking cigar pairs well with bourbon or coffee but can also accompany a full-bodied beer quite nicely. Fans of the original Diesel Whiskey Row and its variants will surely come to enjoy the flavorful profile offered by this modern day masterpiece. Barrel-aged tobacco, world class blending and rolling, and a name that means business—Diesel Whiskey Row Founder’s Collection Raceking is certainly a stick that deserves attention.

Hailing from the Miami-based El Rey de los Habanos factory, the Don Pepin Garcia Black Label cigar, also known as the Cuban Classic, represents one-fifth of the realization of a young boy's dream. Let me explain. Young José Garcia began rolling cigars in Cuba in 1961 when he was just eleven years old, eventually becoming one of the top torcedors in that island country. Thirty years of immersion in the world of the leaf later he fled the Castro regime to make his own fortune, eventually ending up in Miami's Little Havana district where he started his cigar company. To this day, after all of his successes creating cigars for others, only five cigars have earned the right to bear the Don Pepin Garcia name. The all-Nicaraguan Black Label is one of them. Adorned with an elegantly scripted band replacing the more simple label of years past, the rich brown Habano Rosado wrapper firmly embraces expertly bunched fillers that reek with coca-like aromas. When smoked, the first third of the cigar is loaded with coffee and woodsy notes, the perfect draw pumping smoke. Some of the characteristic Don Pepin black pepper enters during the second third right about the time the cigar goes full-throttle, and it keeps the pedal down throughout the last half when some leather and spice are added to the ever-shifting mix. You'll nub this cigar, no doubt. A feast for all five senses. The Don Pepin Garcia Black Label is recommended for more experienced smokers, particularly those who enjoy Joya De Nicaragua Antaño or Cain Habano .

Don Pepin Blue Label is the one that started it all for Jose "Don" Pepin Garcia. Once a master roller in Cuba, Don Pepin has been involved in the business since age 11 and now owns and operates My Father Cigars, a state-of-the-art factory in Nicaragua responsible for some of the most sought-after cigars in the world. Blue Label is his personal favorite blend, using Nicaraguan fillers, Nicaraguan Criollo binders, and Nicaraguan Corojo wrappers. This blend was made to mimic the old time Cubans that Don Pepin grew up with. The elegant blue band hugs the reddish, veiny cigar that is masterfully constructed to have an easy draw from which billowing clouds of bluish gray smoke plentifully flow. From first light, the smoker is greeted by the infamous "Pepin Pepper," a blast of intense spice across the entire palate. The smoke settles into a full-bodied array of nutty and spicy flavors with heavy pepper and sweetness on the finish. This stick is very full-bodied and is by no means a beginner cigar. It pairs well with scotch or bourbon and makes a wonderful weekend smoke for any experienced connoisseur. Comparable cigars include San Cristobal and Don Pepin Black Label—both additional masterpieces blended by Don Pepin himself. It doesn't get much closer to the taste of a full-bodied Cuban than Don Pepin Blue Label.

Don Jose Pepin Garcia is arguably making some of the finest cigars in the world right now. Whether it is with Pete Johnson for Tatuaje, with his son Jaime for My Father, or his own Don Pepin Garcia label, they all have amazing flavor, flawless construction, and copious amounts of smoke. When he came out and said the Serie JJ was the best of all his brands, it was definitely something to take notice of. Made in Miami to the company's highest standards, this Nicaraguan puro has the best filler and binder, and is wrapped with a light Nicaraguan Corojo Rosado wrapper leaf. Medium-to-full in body, Serie JJ hits all the right notes for full flavored cigar lovers. The beautiful white and gold band and secondary Serie JJ label have almost a regal appearance, making us aware from the start we were going to be in for an excellent experience. The first thing we like to do with a smoke is smell the foot, and surprisingly the Serie JJ was lacking any sort of aroma pre-light. Any worry we were about to embark on a flavorless journey was quenched as soon as the flame touched foot. The signature Pepin blast of pepper hit us square in the face, but quickly subsided to reveal a very complex and earthy cigar. Don Pepin Garcia Serie JJ is a fantastic cigar which morphs in flavor with every few puffs. What starts as a full-bodied spicy cigar soon mellows into a medium-to-full-bodied smoke with notes of wood and coffee. The full nature of this cigar lends itself to being enjoyed after a meal and with a nice bitter espresso. Other great cigars to smoke are the Tatuaje Miami or the lighter in body La Duena.

They say the third time's a charm, and Don Pepin Vegas Cubanas proves that this can be true even when it comes to premium cigars. In 2023, the Don Pepin brand celebrated twenty years since its humble beginnings. Back then, Jose "Don" Pepin Garcia and his small team produced cigars in a tiny boutique shop in Miami, nobody imagined that one day their brand would become one of the most dominant monsters the industry has ever seen. One of the first cigars rolled in that small shop was Vegas Cubanas, but unfortunately the brand fizzled out as Don Pepin's other brands took flight. Fast forward to 2017, and we see Don Pepin bring back the brand, this time produced in his massive, world-renowned My Father factory in Nicaragua. The brand took off briefly, even earning some respectable ratings along the way, but history would repeat itself as it died off again a few years later. Then 2023 came along. There was one final attempt to resurrect one of Don Pepin's oldest blends, and this time, he got it right. A Nicaraguan puro, Vegas Cubanas contains all Nicaraguan tobacco—filler, binder, and wrapper. The wrapper leaf is a premium aged Corojo Rosado leaf grown on Don Pepin's own farm. This blend has quickly risen to the top, with a solid 93 rating in Cigar Aficionado and acceptance with open arms from Don Pepin fans the world over. Sometimes in the cigar world, packaging can have a huge impact on how people view the brand, and the folks at My Father Cigars seem to know that. For this installment, the packaging is in line with Don Pepin's other core lines, including Cuban Classic, JJ, and the infamous Blue Label blend. This time, the bands are green and gold, offering a fresh new look and an appropriate theme, as Vegas Cubanas is literally translated "Cuban Farms." The construction is typically high-end, as one would expect from My Father Cigars, meaning a beautiful roll and a Cuban style triple cap. A smooth draw, a sharp burn line, and billowing clouds of silky, thick smoke are constant with each stick. The cigar starts off with a signature Pepin pepper storm, though this one is a bit tamer than most other cigars bearing the My Father name. Quickly, an earthy, woody profile is established, speckled along the way with simple hints of cedar, brown sugar, and coffee. The body is creamy and easy-going, and the finish is crisp and clean, with just a hint of red chili. Simple, yet just complex enough to be interesting throughout, this medium-bodied cigar alludes to many famed Cuban brands of old. Medium-bodied and easy to enjoy, Vegas Cubanas are appropriate for just about anyone. Beginners have nothing to fear in terms of it being overpowering, and established cigar enthusiasts will no doubt appreciate the Cuban style flavor profile. This stick pairs well with coffee, bourbon, or medium-bodied beer and is a great cigar to enjoy any time of the day. Similar in stature to Don Pepin Cuban Classic or My Father Flor de Las Antillas , it is sure to appeal to a very wide variety of cigar nuts. It's safe to say that the new Vegas Cubanas are here to stay, so what are you waiting for? Grab some today and experience the old-fashioned Cuban style flavor that Don Pepin and company have become known for, and all at a fantastic price point.

In 2023, My Father Cigars , formerly known as Don Pepin Garcia Brands, celebrated its 20th anniversary, and to say it was celebrated to great lengths would be an understatement. One of several incredible offerings to come from that lasting celebration was the company’s contribution to the yearly TAA Exclusive Series Program, and a cigar that would become an ongoing celebration of its own: Don Pepin Vintage Edition . Defined by old-school packaging and a retro-style flavor profile , this cigar is made in the world-famous My Father Factory in Nicaragua under the supervision of Jose “Don Pepin” Garcia himself. A Nicaraguan puro to the fullest degree, Vintage Edition uses only the finest all-Nicaraguan tobacco recipe—wrapper, filler, and binder. For a wrapper leaf , the Garcias went with a gorgeous Corojo 99 leaf grown on the family’s own farms. A pair of 90 ratings in Cigar Aficionado right out of the gate kick-started its popularity, but since its debut, this blend has become incredibly popular, especially among Don Pepin’s original audience that enjoyed the early blends back in the day. A cedar cabinet box houses the gorgeous cigars, each one reddish-brown and rolled to surgical standards. The bands are the real standout here, modeled after the very earliest Don Pepin brand nearly a century ago but very similar to the ones worn by the Miami-made original Don Pepin sticks that put the brand on the map in the early 2000s. Maroon and cream is the color profile, and the classic-style band just seems to give the cigar a lovely enigma. Cedar and pepper start things off, along with a definitive toasty note that lingers throughout the transition into the earthy Nicaraguan part of the flavor profile that tends to dominate things for the rest of the smoke. Creamy around the edges, with hints of baking spices and frequent blasts of white pepper , this puro takes you back to some of Don Pepin’s early blends. Oh, and it just wouldn’t be a classic Don Pepin stick if it wasn’t definitively full-bodied , so that part goes without question. Full-bodied, smooth and spicy , and complex to about the same degree as the world’s finest Cubans, Don Pepin Vintage Edition is the quintessential connoisseurs’ cigar . Made for the experienced, this Nicaraguan puro pairs beautifully with your favorite scotch or bourbon but also goes well with coffee or full-bodied beer. Fans of the famed blends that sent My Father Cigars into the big leagues, such as Don Pepin Blue Label or Don Pepin Black Label , will surely want to take a stroll down memory lane while enjoying this potent concoction. Whether you are a long-time fan of Don Pepin cigars or happen to be a seasoned cigar enthusiast that wants to try the hottest sticks out there, enjoying a Don Pepin Vintage Edition is certainly an opportunity you won’t want to pass up.

Carrillo Cigars has had immense success over the past few years, finally coming to a high point by having his ultra-premium Encore named Cigar of the Year, but lurking behind the more popular cigars in the E.P. Carrillo lineup is a truly hidden gem every bit as capable of garnering attention: Capa de Sol. Made by skilled hands in the Dominican Republic at Carrillo's own factory, Capa de Sol is a firecracker of a cigar, using top-grade filler and binder tobacco from Nicaragua and an Ecuadorian Sun Grown wrapper leaf. Ernesto Perez-Carrillo doesn't mess around when he comes out with a new blend, so rest assured that Capa de Sol is built to please. (Shop other E.P. Carrillo Cigars ) Golden brown and oily, Capa de Sol wears an elegant gold and orange band and sports impeccable construction. A gentle roll ensures an easy draw with a ton of smoke output along with a razor sharp burn. Starting off, Capa de Sol is nutty and spicy. Bursts of Nicaraguan white pepper tickle the tongue while a heavy cedar note begins to take over. Earthy tobacco and spicy cayenne contend with each other on the retrohale, and the finish is crisp and clean. Capa de Sol resides on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied, but is beautifully balanced to ensure a velvety smooth experience. Over the years, E.P. Carrillo Cigars has released some of the most sought-after connoisseur cigars on the market. Such sticks as La Historia and the aforementioned Encore were intended for mature audiences, so to speak, as beginners would simply miss out on everything that makes them special. With Capa de Sol, however, we have a medium-full-bodied cigar with plenty of complexity and the balance that Carrillo cigars are so well-known for, yet at a reasonable price point and easily enjoyable for palates of all experience levels. Try pairing Capa de Sol with a medium-bodied beer or red wine to get a luxurious one-two punch of flavor and intensity. Literally translated "Wrapper of the Sun," Capa de Sol is aptly named, as it proves to be one of the hottest offerings from E.P. Carrillo on today's market. Check out other E.P. Carrillo cigars: E.P. A decadent and full-bodied treat, the E.P. Carillo Cardinal Impact Maduro cigar is another hit for its maker. Ernesto Perez-Carillo is renowned for his ability to create small-batch boutique smokes that rival anything the big producers can muster, and the Cardinal line is his gift to aficionados who seek out the heaviest and most robust stogies they can find. With its ligero-laden blend of Nicaraguan filler and toothy Connecticut Broadlead wrapper this is easily the strongest blend to come from Carillo's E.P.C. Cigar company, but the man's genius is on display by not sacrificing complex and satisfying flavor in the quest for more power. (Shop other E.P. Carrillo Cigars ) Providing leathery, spicy flavors punctuated with notes of oak wine barrel, cinnamon, and cream, the cigar stays cool burning and sweet to the end. For those not quite ready to take on the Cardinal Impact Maduro, some of Ernesto's other creations offer the perfect opportunity to experience his talents. Fans of mild cigars will love the New Wave Connecticut while those who prefer bolder smokes should go for the Core Line Maduro. Ready to go all out? Order some Cardinal Maduros today and get ready to be amazed by its strengths. Check out other E.P. Carrillo cigars: E.P. Carrillo Allegiance E.P. Carrillo Capa De Sol E.P. The E.P. Carillo Cardinal Natural cigar fills the one remaining gap left by the other fantastic smokes coming out of the E.P.C. Cigar company. From the mild and oh-so-tasty New Wave Connecticut to the medium-strength Core Line and Inch and even the more robust Elencos, there had not been an E.P. Carillo branded stick aimed squarely at the heart of those who favor full-bore strength and taste in their cigars. The Cardinal Natural corrects this, being billed as the most full-bodied in their lineup and boy does it deliver. A rich and creamy blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican tobaccos was expertly blended to meld with the peppery Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper to become the cigar that dreams are made of.(Shop other E.P. Carrillo Cigars ) Just in case you're unfamiliar with what Ernesto Perez-Carillo is capable of when it comes to full bodied smokes, check out the La Gloria Cubana Serie N and Serie R. The Cardinal Natural is easily on the same level and might even be Carillo's best ever with a profile awash in brown sugar, charred wood, sweet biscuit, and dark fruit prevalent from the beginning through to the cool burning nub. For deepest satisfaction, pair with a spiced rum, a hammock, and a warm afternoon. Just be prepared to stay put. Check out other E.P. Carrillo cigars: E.P. Carrillo Allegiance E.P. Ernesto Perez-Carrillo is a master of Maduro who has created some of your favorite dark cigars over the years, but the E.P. Carrillo Core Plus Maduro might just be the best of them all. After finding fame and fortune with the ever-popular La Gloria Cubana line, the time came for Ernesto to return to his roots as head of a boutique brand, this time heralding his name. A slew of highly-rated and award-winning smokes soon followed, but Ernesto knew what the world really wanted from him was a Maduro. To that end, he crafted blend after blend until finding just the right combination of Nicaraguan tobaccos to pair with an Ecuadorian binder to create the perfect foundation for the expertly fermented American Connecticut Broadleaf used as the wrapper. Oily, ebony in color, and with a rich tobacco aroma, the Broadleaf wrapper that coats each muscular vitola seems nearly overflowing with juicy filler. Silky to the touch while hiding the few visible veins and seams with precision, an E.P. Carrillo Core Plus Maduro provides a smooth and steady cold draw which both preps the palate with hints of minerals and chocolate and shows the care with which each and every torcedor employed at his Tabacalera La Alianza factory fulfills Ernesto's vision. Frontloaded with coffee beans, dark cocoa, and a hint of cherry, the profile nonetheless remains a steady medium in body. It does ramp up slightly near the finale, after leather, cinnamon, maple syrup, and cedar have all had a chance to impress. It's truly amazing that in this day and age, a cigar of this magnitude can be had for less than double digits. But that's the way Ernesto rolls, if you'll excuse the pun. Fill that empty space in your humidor and your life with as many E.P. Carrillo Core Plus Maduros as you can get away with. We guarantee they're worth it. Check out other E.P. Carrillo cigars: E.P. When it comes down to it, all we cigar smokers want is the pure essence of great tobacco, and the E.P. Carrillo Core Plus Natural just so happens to provide exactly what we're looking for. Being able to consistently create some of the world's best cigars is a skill that cannot be attained on a whim, but the famed Ernesto Perez-Carrillo is up to the task. Easily bearing the weight of four generations of Cuban cigar-makers, this master of the stogie has summoned a blend of Nicaraguan longleaf aged three to five years to serve as the core (ahem) of the Core Plus Natural. Such an exquisite recipe requires a wrapper equal in stature, and so a creamy Ecuadorian-grown Sumatra wrapper was added to the team. The result is an instant medium to full strength classic. For anyone familiar with Ernesto's cigars, one of the hallmarks of the many brands he has shepherded into our humidors over the years is the remarkable consistency in quality and skill evident in each well-packed barrel. The E.P Carrillo Core Plus Natural is no exception. Concealing a remarkable wealth of filler tobaccos regardless of vitola, the Sumatra wrapper exudes a sharp cedar aroma while the foot wafts cocoa and almond. After lighting, the pleasure of watching thick clouds of aromatic smoke burst from your lips will compete with the palate's thrill at tasting not just the trademark creamy cedar and warm spice found in most Carrillo sticks, but also cocoa, molasses, loam, black coffee, and hints of dried fruit.

Few cigar makers have reached the pinnacle of the premium cigar industry quite like Ernesto Perez-Carrillo. With award-winning blends such as La Historia, Pledge, and the legendary Encore, named Cigar Aficionado's 2018 #1 Cigar of the Year , Carrillo has built a legacy on craftsmanship, innovation, and an unwavering pursuit of perfection. Never one to rest on past success, Ernesto returned to the celebrated Encore blend with a new objective: create a darker, richer, and more powerful expression worthy of carrying the Encore name. The result is the E.P. Carrillo Encore Black . Handcrafted in the Dominican Republic, the Encore Black revolves around an exceptional Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper that undergoes an extraordinary 18 months of fermentation followed by three years of bale aging before ever touching a rolling table. This painstaking process unlocks the wrapper's remarkable richness while preserving its natural complexity. Beneath it lies a flavorful Mexican San Andrés binder and a carefully balanced blend of premium Nicaraguan fillers from Condega, Estelí, and Jalapa , creating a medium-to-full-bodied profile that is both bold and refined. Construction is everything cigar enthusiasts have come to expect from the Carrillo family. The draw is effortless, the burn is razor-sharp, and each puff delivers dense clouds of smoke. The flavor journey begins with rich dark chocolate, black pepper, and toasted oak , gradually unfolding into layers of espresso , earth, and natural tobacco sweetness . Hints of leather and baking spice emerge as the cigar develops, while the extensively aged Broadleaf wrapper ties everything together with a smooth, lingering finish that showcases both power and elegance. Produced in limited quantities, the E.P. Carrillo Encore Black represents the next evolution of one of the most celebrated cigar lines of the modern era. It offers a fuller-bodied experience than the original Encore while preserving the balance, sophistication, and impeccable craftsmanship that define every Carrillo creation. Whether you're already a devoted Encore fan or simply searching for your next standout Broadleaf cigar, Encore Black delivers a performance worthy of its name, an encore you'll gladly experience again and again.

EP Carrillo Essence Sumatra combines classic Carrillo-style flavor with the modern style of blending that took the humble cigar brand to the top of the world. From the classic La Gloria Cubana to the award-winning Carrillo series, Ernesto Perez-Carrillo now has one of the most decorated resumes of anyone in the cigar business. Essence Sumatra can be thought of as a culmination of everything he has been responsible for over the years. Made at the renowned Casa Carrillo factory in the Dominican Republic, this succulent creation is constructed by some of the most skilled artisans the world has to offer. The blend is simple and straightforward, somewhat of a time warp for Carrillo. The filler is Nicaraguan and Dominican, the double binder is from Nicaragua and Honduras, and the wrapper is, you guessed it, Ecuadorian Sumatra. Carrillo has been known for taking the Sumatra leaf to new heights and doing incredible things with it. Such is easily demonstrated by the cigar in question. The conservative, yet dapper packaging for this series includes a clean-cut cedar chest, a black foot band on each vitola, and a very lovely and modern black, gold, and red main band bearing the unmistakable EP Carrillo seal. Construction is always immaculate, leaving nothing to desire. An easy and productive draw slathers the palate with smoke one each puff, dazzling the senses with everything good that can come from an ultra-premium cigar. Cedar and white pepper open the flavor profile, quickly joined by a very prominent almond note that remains throughout. The core is earthy and displays a classic raw tobacco flavor profile, and the finish is sweet, hinted with brown sugar and cinnamon. Medium-bodied, this cigar is about as classic as you can get for a new cigar on today’s market. Made for connoisseurs, but suitable for just about anyone, Essence Sumatra is versatile, refined, and utterly satisfying each and every time. Medium-bodied and delightfully complex, it pairs beautifully with scotch or bourbon, but also goes great with your favorite dark beer. Fans of the classic La Gloria Cubana blend that Carrillo became so well-known for should definitely look into this, but keep in mind, this might be your new favorite! The story of EP Carrillo is one of the most fascinating of anyone in the business, and with cigars like EP Carrillo Essence Sumatra, it’s a sure thing that he’s not done yet!

Ernestso Perez-Carrillo announced in early 2024 that his next big project was to be called the Essence Series, and the ultimate goal was to introduce a lineup of premium cigars using various wrappers and tobaccos of various origins. First came the celebrated Sumatra, followed by the unmistakable Maduro, and now we have this beautiful specimen: The long-awaited EP Carrillo Honduras. As its name would suggest, this blend showcases everything that is amazing and delicious about Honduran tobacco, and it is a bit of a rarity, as it isn’t every day that Carrillo and his team toy with tobacco from this growing region. Another different fact about this cigar is that it is made by hand at Tabacos de Oriente in Honduras, far from EP Carrillo’s own Dominican mega-factory. For this cigar, we have aged Honduran and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos, a Honduran binder, and a gorgeous Olancho San Augustin wrapper leaf from Honduras that has undergone over 2 years of aging and fermentation. This luxurious package demonstrates the impeccable blending prowess of one of the most decorated blenders in the industry and has already proven to be a treat well worth waiting for. Packaged in a clean-cut cedar chest adorned with colorful decoration, EP Carrillo Honduras looks every bit as good as it tastes. Each vitola wears a stylish blue and red band with gold accents bearing the unforgettable EP Carrillo logo. The construction is top-notch on each and every stick, as would be expected for any product bearing the name of the Godfather of Cigars. A crisp burn, easy draw, and a plethora of voluminous blue smoke make for a truly enjoyable experience from start to finish. The journey starts with a definitive note of oak and pepper, soon evolving into a creamy array of spicy chili pepper, dark chocolate, and earth. A faint presence of citrus flavor lingers in the background, something common among cigars using aged Honduran tobacco. The finish is spicy and clean, and overall, this cigar finishes just past the point of medium-bodied, leaning toward the stronger end. Medium-bodied, full-flavored, and delicately balanced, EP Carrillo Honduras is a cigar worthy of a spot in any seasoned connoisseur’s humidor. The beauty of it is that even though it is a true premium cigar, the flavor profile is straightforward enough that even less-experienced cigar enthusiasts can enjoy its easy-going demeanor and use it as a steppingstone on the venture into the world of stronger Honduran cigars. It pairs well with bourbon, scotch, or medium-bodied beer and is a delight to enjoy at any time of the day. Fans of famed Honduran sticks such as Camacho Corojo or the original Punch will likely be taken for a stroll down memory lane as they enjoy the incredible nuances that only a premium Honduran cigar can offer. EP Carrillo never ceases to amaze us as he introduces the cigar world to new and exciting things on what seems like a daily basis. Enjoy the latest from this dominant force in the cigar world with EP Carrillo Honduras, and we promise you’ll be back for more.

Released in Europe with the Cabinet Series at the end of 2014, the E.P. Carrillo New Wave Reserva is slowly making its way stateside as well. This great new release from the mind that brought us La Gloria Cubana is a fantastic medium-bodied smoke worthy of the famed brand name. Much like the original New Wave cigars from Carrillo this cigar uses the same flawless Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. Just like all cigars by E.P. Carrillo, the New Wave Reserva is made with the utmost of quality and consistency. Flavor notes of spice and cedar will dance across your tongue before flame is even introduced. The black pepper spice is quickly subdued after lit, and plays off the natural earthiness within the filler leaves. The perfect burn ensures that each puff is giving you the exact taste of each and every leaf in this fantastic blend. E.P. Carrillo New Wave Reserva was originally released in Europe, but we are glad it is coming to the American marketplace. Each puff is exactly what one should expect from a medium-bodied cigar. This is another winner from the brilliant mind of Ernesto Carrillo. We would also recommend the original E.P. Carrillo New Wave Connecticut as well for a slightly different flavor profile. Few cigars have earned the acclaim of the original E.P. Carrillo Pledge, crowned Cigar Aficionado's 2020 #1 Cigar of the Year with an extraordinary 98 rating. For most manufacturers, such success would be impossible to follow. Ernesto Perez-Carrillo, however, had a different vision. Anticipating the blend's remarkable potential, he set aside select bales of the original Connecticut-grown Habano wrapper for additional aging, patiently waiting years for the tobacco to reveal even greater depth and complexity. The result is the E.P. Carrillo Pledge Purple , a limited-production masterpiece created to celebrate the fifth anniversary of one of the most celebrated cigars of the modern era. Handcrafted at the renowned Casa Carrillo factory in the Dominican Republic, Pledge Purple begins with that beautifully aged Connecticut-grown Habano wrapper harvested from the very same crop as the original Pledge. Beneath it lies a flavorful Mexican binder surrounding a carefully refined blend of premium Nicaraguan fillers from Estelí, Condega, and Ometepe. While inspired by its award-winning predecessor, the internal recipe has been completely reimagined to complement the wrapper's extended maturation, creating a cigar that stands confidently on its own. Construction is immaculate, producing an effortless draw, a razor-sharp burn, and dense clouds of rich smoke. The first puffs unveil bold notes of dark cocoa, espresso, and aged oak , followed by layers of earth, leather, and black pepper that gradually unfold throughout the smoke. Subtle natural sweetness and a creamy texture soften the cigar's full-bodied character, resulting in a profile that is remarkably balanced, refined, and deeply satisfying from beginning to end. As part of Casa Carrillo's exclusive Premier Collection, the E.P. Carrillo Pledge Purple is produced in extremely limited quantities , with only 3,500 boxes released in carefully scheduled installments. It is more than a commemorative release—it is a testament to patience, craftsmanship, and Ernesto Perez-Carrillo's relentless pursuit of perfection. For longtime fans of the original Pledge or collectors searching for one of the year's most anticipated limited editions, the Pledge Purple is a rare opportunity to experience one of the finest expressions the Carrillo family has ever created.

After the amazing La Historia, which was named the #2 Cigar of 2014, it is hard to believe the E.P. Carrillo could make another premium cigar to live up to it. Seleccion Oscuro cigars do just that, and if you are a lover of dark leafed Maduro cigars, may have even surpassed them. These beautiful sticks are wrapped in a unique, thinner Mexican San Andres Oscuro wrapper from the middle priming of the plant. This dark and oily leaf covers an Ecuadorian binder and fine aged Nicaraguan filler tobaccos which offer the smoker a medium-to-full bodied cigar. (Shop other E.P. Carrillo Cigars ) E.P. Carrillo Seleccion Oscuro cigars have a flawless dark Oscuro wrapper that is not just beautiful to look at, but the wrapper also has an amazing pre-light aroma of cedar and earth. After lighting, there is a distinct pepperiness that will cross your lips. Surprisingly for a cigar this dark, there is no prevalent sweetness from the wrapper leaf, and instead, the cedar and earth from the aroma carry on throughout the length of the cigar. E.P.Carillo has been making great cigars for a very long time. From his most famous La Gloria Cubana to his newest creations, these E.P. Carillo Seleccion Oscuro cigars, you can rest assured that each and every puff is going to be full of flavor and perfect construction. After taking the cigar world by storm as a young man, Christian Eiroa took a short but well-deserved hiatus from tobacco before roaring back onto the scene with his Eiroa Classic. Once the fresh-faced prodigy who brought his family's Camacho brand to world renown, Christian is now a (slightly) older man back at the helm of a Honduran cigar company blending the finest longleaf Puros like it ain't no thing. It should come as no surprise then that this full-bodied cigar, which contains hand-picked and extra-aged homegrown leaves, has already garnered a Best-of-the-Year honor. Foregoing any need to dress the cigars in anything fancy or overbearing, Christian has outfitted his Eiroa Classics in a simple red and gold band emblazoned with his name and personal motto of 'Salud Amor Pesetas', meaning 'Health, Love, Money'. Beneath the band, each mouthwatering and golden-brown vitola is solid in construction and without visible veins or flaws. A pre-light preview offers hints of the rich earth and sweet spices that form the foundation of the profile once the cigar is alight. Building on this base, the smoke draws from a deep well of flavor throughout the long burn, delivering bucketloads of black pepper, creamy leather, cedar, marzipan, Dutch cocoa, and citrus straight to the delighted palate. Whether named as a callback to an earlier time or an attempt by Christian to remain humble, we think the Eiroa Classic cigar is appropriately monikered for a variety of reasons. The least of these is the amazing low price for an amazingly delightful and delicious stogie. Fans of immense strength and character should be all over these, like right now. Why are you still thinking about it?

Eiroa The First 20 Years is the special blend that industry megastar Christian Eiroa and his father put together to celebrate his first two decades in the cigar business. The Eiroa family purchased Camacho Cigars in 1995, grew the company, and became known for their ultra-full-bodied cigars and unmatched quality. Coming up with the company, it can be said that Eiroa learned a thing or two about blending and producing premium cigars. In the early 2000s Camacho Cigars was sold to Davidoff and Christian Eiroa wasted no time introducing his own brand, CLE Cigars, the flagship cigar simply being called Eiroa. Eiroa The First 20 Years takes that flagship name to a whole new level, and is among his crowning achievements to date. This incredible puro hails from Honduras and boasts a robust blend of all-Honduran tobacco—wrapper, filler, and binder, grown in the beautiful Jamastran Valley. This tobacco is all but ordinary, however, as the stash used for these stogies is an heirloom crop that hasn't been used in over 50 years. The end result can be thought of as a throwback to the premium Camachos of old, with a bit more refinement, but just as much raw strength as all true Camacho fans have come to know and love from their cigars. Apparently the folks at Cigar Aficionado love this particular blend, as it recently earned a solid 92 rating. Dark and oily, road-mapped with veins, and sporting a very pronounced box press, Eiroa The First 20 Years wears a similar gold on red band to the original Eiroa line, along with an elegant tissue wrapper on the bottom half. Construction-wise, expect what has always been expected for a cigar rolled under Christian Eiroa's supervision: an easy draw, crisp, sharp burn, and absolutely incredible consistency from cigar to cigar. Dense, thick plumes of silky white smoke pound the palate hard with earthy tobacco flavor and spicy white pepper. Definitive notes of cedar and nuts adorn the flavor profile, along with leathery nuances and hints of cayenne. Sweet cocoa lingers in the background as the cigar progresses, and the finish is smooth, yet intense. A rock-solid full-bodied stick from beginning to end, Eiroa The First 20 Years is not for the faint of heart. Strong and complex, perfectly balanced, and incomparably satisfying, Eiroa The First 20 Years is a connoisseurs' level cigar that has no doubt already made its mark in the industry. It demands to be enjoyed slowly and passionately, in order to truly appreciate every twist and turn throughout the intense experience. This puro pairs nicely with bourbon, tawny port, or a simple cup of coffee, and is a must-try for fans of the old fashioned Camacho cigars. Eiroa The First 20 Years joins Asylum , Asylum 13 , CLE Prieto , and the other incredible blends from the former Camacho head honcho, and is currently the most sought-after blend of the bunch. With this cigar, Christian Eiroa celebrated his first 20 years in the business. What will you be celebrating as you enjoy the smooth, powerful journey that is Eiroa The First 20 Years?

note_sources.text: Though newer cigar enthusiasts may not realize it, El Rey del Mundo was once one of the biggest names in the world of premium cigars. A dominant force during the Cigar Boom era, El Rey del Mundo eventually settled toward the bottom of an ever-growing list of premium cigars that now steal the spotlight. However, the Honduran giant isn’t dead yet. Not long ago, a dazzling new addition was made to the brand’s portfolio: El Rey del Mundo Shade Grown . Made in Honduras, this is the first El Rey del Mundo ever to be wrapped in a Connecticut-seed wrapper. This wrapper leaf is grown under shade in Honduras’s Talanga Valley. It is then combined with a Honduran Jamastran binder and Honduran fillers from Jamastran and Copan. This stick, therefore, is a Honduran puro—an unusual one, as Honduras isn’t typically known for producing Connecticut-seed wrappers. Classic cedar chests house the precision-built vitolas, each one bearing the unmistakable El Rey del Mundo gold-on-gold band. A secondary “Shade Grown” band distinguishes this particular variant. Designed to perform, El Rey del Mundo Shade Grown offers a smooth and productive draw while holding a long, firm ash. Beginning with a bold cedar flavor, the cigar transitions into a creamy medley of cinnamon, cocoa, and brown sugar. A grassy undertone weaves throughout, balancing the sweetness and adding an earthy backbone to the profile. Mild to medium-bodied, this cigar is as easy on the palate as it is on the wallet. Ideal for beginners, loved by connoisseurs, El Rey del Mundo Shade Grown is an extremely versatile cigar. Mellow, mild, and delightfully flavorful, this stick pairs well with white wine, bourbon, or even a simple cup of coffee. Fans of milder Connecticut cigars such as Perdomo Champagne or Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real will likely enjoy the calm and easy-going nature of this particular offering. El Rey del Mundo, as a brand, may not be as popular as it once was, but with cigars like El Rey del Mundo Shade Grown, we are reminded that sometimes the classics can surprise us, even in today’s unbelievably competitive cigar industry.

It’s always exciting when a well-known celebrity gets involved with a cigar brand, especially when that brand happens to be one of the best in the business. In early 2022, photos of Erik Espinosa of Espinosa Cigars and celebrity chef/television personality Guy Fieri sparked a frenzy of social media speculation about the two doing a project together. It wasn’t long before that project came to fruition. Behold, Espinosa Knuckle Sandwich Habano ! This is actually the 92-rated blend that put the Knuckle Sandwich series on the map, earning a spot on Cigar Aficionado’s Top 25 of 2022 . There have since been several releases, now totaling 5 different blends within the Knuckle Sandwich umbrella. This knockout stogie is made by the skilled hands at the world-famous San Lotano factory in Nicaragua, overseen by none other than AJ Fernandez himself. Nicaraguan fillers combine with a Nicaraguan binder, and the wrapper is a gorgeous reddish-hued Habano leaf grown in Ecuador. With so many names involved in one cigar brand, one would expect something huge. Well, you’ve got it! Shiny, clean red cedar chests house the precision-built vitolas, and each one sports a black and gold band and a tidy black ribbon around the foot. Made for optimal performance, Knuckle Sandwich doesn’t play around when it comes to smoke production, and the output is phenomenal. White pepper and cedar open things up, but soon a tongue-tickling array of almond, cinnamon, and cocoa spices things up. Earthy to the core and boasting a backbone of spicy Nicaraguan flavor , this explosive concoction finishes on the heavy end of medium-full-bodied . Purely balanced and delicately complex, it’s easy to see how a famed chef was quick to put his name behind this one. Made for the experienced , Knuckle Sandwich Habano is a top-rated treat that is sure to satisfy any experienced fan of medium-full-bodied, complex cigars. Pair this one with your favorite medium-full-bodied beer, bourbon, or even some of Guy Fieri’s famous Tequila, and enjoy a trip to Flavorville, USA. Fans of such sticks as San Lotano or 601 Red Label are sure to take a liking to this one, along with anyone that simply loves a cigar that tells a story with its flavor profile. You don’t have to be a chef to know good flavor when it’s there. One taste of Knuckle Sandwich Habano and you’re sure to see what you’ve been missing all this time.

When Erik Espinosa and AJ Fernandez teamed up with celebrity chef Guy Fieri to make the original Knuckle Sandwich, there was little doubt that it would be a hit, but few would have guessed it would come this far. In 2025, however, some three years after the original came into existence, the one that many would call the best of the bunch made its debut: Knuckle Sandwich Puro Nicaragua . Like its sister cigars, Puro Nicaragua is made at Fernandez’s San Lotano factory in Nicaragua. This one differs from the others, however, in that every single leaf used in its production is grown and cultivated in Nicaragua, wrapper, filler, and binder. Blended to be a bit stronger than the others, this variation seems to be geared even more towards the seasoned connoisseur. Numerous 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado prove that this stick is more than worthy of being part of the Knuckle Sandwich series. The wooden chest is rustic and the black, red, and silver bands adorning each cigar come together to give serious biker bar vibes. Each box-pressed vitola bears the all-too-recognizable skull in a chef’s hat, and each stick wears a silver band at the foot. An easy, productive draw offers plenty of smoke, and the opening is spicy and meaty . A nice dose of white pepper opens things up, followed by a cascade of rich Nicaraguan tobacco goodness. Notes of nutmeg and cinnamon are detectable, but the main core is toasty and rich. A dose of cedar and spice on the finish wraps things up, and all-in-all Knuckle Sandwich Puro Nicaragua finishes strong at the heavy end of medium-full bodied . Made for the experienced, Knuckle Sandwich Puro Nicaragua is built from the ground up to cover all the bases. Strong, complex, balanced, and smooth, this medium-full-bodied masterpiece is sure to impress any fan of spicy Nicaraguan cigars. While this one pairs well with your favorite scotch or bourbon, black coffee makes a fine accompaniment as well. If you tried the Knuckle Sandwich Habano and took a liking to it, you certainly owe it to yourself to give this one a try. Fieri, Espinosa, and Fernandez have done it again, and this time it’s bolder than ever. Try an Espinosa Knuckle Sandwich Puro Nicaragua today and experience the true greatness of a Nicaraguan puro.
Leather , Earth , Hazelnut , Molasses Drink. Crafted with precision and wrapped in a decadent Maduro broadleaf, Excalibur Maduro is the perfect follow-up to the classic Excalibur

Just one Connecticut Broadleaf wasn't enough to contain the chocolaty goodness packed into the Hoyo de Monterrey Excalibur Maduro cigar so General Cigar added a second as the binder. The result is an earthy, medium-bodied cigar that it is complex and creamy in all the right ways. The recipient of a Cigar Aficionado top-25 in 2007, this smoke still compares favorably with many of today's popular brands and stands as a preeminent example of a solid, classic Honduran maduro. It certainly doesn't hurt that the three-country filler tobaccos beneath the dual Connies are the direct descendants of the seed Estelo Padron smuggled out of Cuba after the revolution. The flavor is rich with cocoa and coffee, yet at the same time tangy and sweet. 90+ rated and amazingly affordable, you can't afford to not have a box comfortably aging right now for future enjoyment. Just don't expect to have them sitting in your humidor for that long, but they're so good you won't mind buying them again and again. Luckily, these cigars have staying power so they should be around to satisfy for years to come.

The Hoyo de Monterrey Excalibur Natural cigar is a perfectly balanced smoke, offering clean, flavorful tobacco brought to life through time-honored aging and rolling techniques. Building on the already exquisite Hoyo de Monterrey Natural, the master blenders at General Cigar created the Excalibur line using only the finest tobaccos, selected for their smooth and mellow character. With a paired Connecticut shade wrapper and binder to temper the hearty blend of Honduran, Nicaraguan, and Dominican filler, the cigar maintains plenty of complexity and a satisfying kick for even the most discerning aficionados. This blend has been rated 91 by Cigar Aficionado . The twin Connecticut leaves provide a solid canvas for the rich flavors that emerge upon lighting: notes of leather and espresso dominate the opening, while the second third introduces a honeyed sweetness that excites the palate. As the cigar approaches the nub, layers of nutmeg and allspice add a refined spice to the experience. Medium-bodied and approachable for any smoker who appreciates classic tobacco flavors crafted by skilled artisans, the Excalibur is both affordable and rewarding. Fans of Connecticut-wrapped cigars, from the mild Cusano 18 to the more robust Berger & Argenti Entubar, will find much to enjoy here. Pair it with a cold lager or iced tea and savor the finer things in life.

The Ferio Tego Metropolitan Host completes the revival of a classic lineup, bringing back one of the most approachable and beloved blends from the original Metropolitan portfolio. Carefully preserved by Michael Herklots and Brendan Scott, this blend remains true to its roots, offering the same smooth, easygoing character that made it a staple for everyday enjoyment. Handcrafted in Honduras, the Metropolitan Host feature a silky Connecticut Shade wrapper over a core of Honduran binder and long-filler tobaccos, creating a mild, creamy profile with exceptional balance. Finished with a lightly sweetened cap, this cigar delivers a touch of added sweetness that enhances, rather than overwhelms, the natural tobacco flavors. From the first draw, expect a soft, inviting profile layered with notes of cream, light cedar, and subtle cocoa , complemented by a gentle natural sweetness . As the cigar develops, hints of leather, soft spice, and toasted nuts emerge, all wrapped in a smooth, mellow texture that remains consistent from start to finish. The finish is clean, slightly sweet , and satisfying. Designed for versatility and ease of enjoyment, the Metropolitan Host are an ideal choice for a morning smoke, a casual afternoon break, or a relaxing evening wind-down. Smooth, balanced, and highly approachable, it stands as a perfect everyday cigar—one that delivers classic flavor with a modern touch of sweetness.

The Ferio Tego Metropolitan Maduro continues the legacy of a beloved classic, reintroduced for today’s smokers with the same blend integrity that made it a staple in humidors for years. Originally part of the Nat Sherman portfolio, this time-tested Maduro has been carefully preserved by Michael Herklots and Brendan Scott, delivering a familiar, refined experience with a deeper, richer profile. Handcrafted in Honduras, the Metropolitan Maduro features a dark, flavorful Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over a core of Honduran binder and long-filler tobaccos, resulting in a smooth, medium-bodied cigar with added depth and character. From the first draw, expect a warm and inviting profile layered with notes of earth, cocoa, and toasted nuts , complemented by a natural sweetness that lingers on the palate. As the cigar develops, flavors of coffee, light spice, and cream emerge, creating a balanced interplay between richness and smoothness. Despite its dark Maduro appearance, the body remains approachable, offering complexity without heaviness. Consistent, flavorful, and easy to enjoy, the Metropolitan Maduro is a versatile cigar suited for both newer smokers exploring Maduro profiles and seasoned aficionados seeking a reliable, everyday option. Whether paired with coffee or dark rum, or simply enjoyed on its own, it delivers a satisfying experience rooted in tradition and craftsmanship.

While Ferio Tego Timeless Panamericana may be a relatively new cigar brand, it has actually been around for over a decade. Originally released in 2014 as an exclusive for the Nat Sherman Townhouse, the brand’s signature store located in Manhattan, this cigar became a nationwide offering just 4 years later, though still only at Nat Sherman retailers. Fast forward, and it is now a permanent part of the Ferio Tego portfolio, available for whoever wants it. Timeless Panamericana is produced by the skilled artisans at the world renowned Plasencia Cigars S.A. in Esteli, Nicaragua, and the original recipe remains the same to this day. That recipe includes a filler blend from Costa Rica and Nicaragua, a Nicaraguan binder, and a beautiful Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Old school appeal meets modern blending here, and the result is spectacular. So much so, in fact, that Timeless Panamericana has earned numerous 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado since its re-release. The cedar chest housing the cigars is stunning. The cigars, each wearing black and gold double bands, almost appear too beautiful to smoke. The main band displaying the “Timeless” logo is quite reminiscent of the classic Nat Sherman version of this stick, and to anyone not paying close attention, they might think that’s what they’re getting. But low and behold, this Plasencia-made gem of a cigar is built for maximum performance, offering an easy draw and a razor-sharp burn every time. White pepper greets the palate with authority on the opening puffs, but the smoke soon settles into an earthy array of cedar, nuts, and rich raw tobacco flavor. A crisp backbone of spice holds the flavor profile together, and the finish is smooth and peppery. Medium-full-bodied and just complex enough to keep any connoisseur on their toes, Timeless Panamericana is certainly a cigar that you won’t forget. Made for seasoned cigar veterans, Timeless Panamericana is a cigar that can truly be considered “ultra-premium.” Medium-full-bodied, intensely flavorful, and satisfying to the max, this refined Nicaraguan heavy hitter is loved by aficionados all over the world. It is wonderfully paired with scotch or bourbon, but a simple cup of black coffee compliments it just fine. Fans of Nicaraguan flavor bombs such as My Father or Aging Room Quattro Nicaragua will likely enjoy the spicy, earthy attributes this stick has to offer. The folks at Ferio Tego couldn’t have come up with a better name for this blend. It is everything any cigar fanatic could want, and it has certainly stood the test of time. Ferio Tego Timeless Panamericana is truly a cigar that is, well, timeless!

In recent years, there has been a trend of celebrated cigar brands coming “back from the dead,” and one cluster of cigars that has proven hugely successful is the Timeless blends by Ferio Tego, formerly sold under the Nat Sherman umbrella. This specimen, Ferio Tego Timeless Sterling, resurrects the beloved Nat Sherman Sterling cigar that was once such a treasure in the humidors of many a connoisseur. This blend is made at the famed Quesada factory in the Dominican Republic using a heavily aged blend of Dominican filler and binder tobaccos. The finishing touch is a golden-brown Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper leaf. Of the four different variants in the Timeless series, Sterling is easily the most recognizable, and it certainly provides a nostalgic experience for those who enjoyed the blend in the Nat Sherman era. Black and silver boxes done with modern décor house the beautifully hand-crafted vitolas. A gold main band with the unmistakable Timeless logo is followed by a golden secondary bearing the Ferio Tego name. Construction is precise, allowing for a seamless and enjoyable smoking experience each and every time. A productive draw offers no shortage in smoke production, and the first flavors to greet the palate are nuts and herbs. This flavorful opening is soon followed by an array of black pepper and cedar, and a smoky, spicy finish rolls out of the nose on the retrohale. A sweet floral note lingers in the background, and after all is said and done Timeless Sterling finishes as a medium-bodied cigar. Made for true connoisseurs, Timeless Sterling has all the attributes that a classic high-end cigar would be known for. Delicately complex flavor, medium body with a creamy texture, and beautiful balance and construction make this treat something to look forward to. It pairs well with bourbon or scotch and can certainly be used for any of life’s celebratory purposes. Fans of sticks such as Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real or Montecristo Classic will surely enjoy the familiar flavor profile provided by such a rich Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper leaf. The Timeless blends are back, and they seem to be living up to their name! Enjoy a Ferio Tego Timeless Sterling today and soak in all the opulent characteristics that only a true classic premium cigar can provide.

After the demise of the Nat Sherman cigar lineup in 2019, many long-time fans were a bit disheartened, to say the least. That’s when former Nat Sherman executives Michael Herklots and Brendon Scott stepped up to the plate, bought rights to the two biggest lines (Timeless and Metropolitan Selection), and kept the heartbeat of the projects going, now sold under the new brand name, Ferio Tego . Though all the Timeless variants have done exceptionally well, one seems to stand out just a little in front of the rest: Timeless Supreme . This Nicaraguan puro, made by the Plasencia family down in sunny Nicaragua, contains 100% Nicaraguan tobacco through and through—wrapper, filler, and binder. This top-grade tobacco is grown on the Plasencia farms and delicately aged and cured to be used in only the finest projects, and we assure you; this one certainly qualifies. The Timeless Supreme turned out so well it earned a stellar 95 rating in Cigar Aficionado and #10 Cigar of the Year by Cigar Aficionado , and appropriately so. Black-topped cedar chests house the gorgeous box-pressed works of fine tobacco art, each one dressed in double black and gold bands. Precision rolling provides a phenomenal smoking experience every time, with an easy and productive draw offering immense clouds of dense smoke from each puff. Spicy white pepper and a hint of herbs opens things up. Soon after, the earthy raw tobacco backbone makes its presence felt, becoming the dominant part of the flavor profile. Notes of cinnamon, leather, and cedar are easily detectable, and the finish is crisp and toasty. When all is said and done, Timeless Supreme finishes as a stout full-bodied cigar. Made for those with years of experience, Timeless Supreme is nothing short of a connoisseur-level cigar. Full-bodied and complex, with well-rounded twists and turns throughout the flavor profile, this rich treat leaves very little to be desired. It pairs well with bourbon or scotch, but a hot cup of black coffee makes for a lovely pairing as well. If you’ve already re-visited the Nat Sherman era by enjoying Timeless Sterling or Timeless Panamericana , you definitely owe it to yourself to give this edition a try. Maybe you are an old school Nat Sherman fan. Maybe you just like full-bodied sticks that are made with some of the world’s finest tobacco. Maybe you just like sticks with cool bands and boxes. No matter how you put it, Ferio Tego Timeless Supreme is a cigar that is doubtless going to leave a good impression.

The new Flor De Las Antillas Maduro cigar has a lot of legacy to live up to, what with coming from the venerable My Father Cigars and all that, but it handles the pressure cool as a cucumber. Never mind that the natural-wrapped version of this blend was named #1 Cigar of the Year in 2012. Pass over the fact that the near-twin My Father Le Bijou 1922 won the same honor in 2015. Here we stand at the dawn of a new day, the moment of opportunity for the Ecuadorian-grown Habano Sun Grown Oscuro wrapper to shine a light all its own onto the masses of eager smokers chomping at the bit. How will the savory and robust Nicaraguan fillers and binders, sourced from three of the Garcia family's best farms, react to the newcomer? They rise to the occasion, of course. Sniffed straight from the humidor, the broad and red-banded foot of the Flor De Las Antillas Maduro cigar allows earthy, woody aromas to flow from the thickly layered tobaccos within, while the shimmering Oscuro wrapper smells more of fresh hay and chocolate. The gorgeously decorated primary label is an instant classic, while impeccable rolling technique pleases the eye, the hand, the lips. Crisp yet robust from the moment it is lit, the smoke pours from the cigar lush with spice, oak, dark berries, cocoa, and salt. Further expansion of flavor will seem impossible until later appearances of black coffee, leather, citrus, and red licorice fill the mouth and the nose with wave after creamy wave of delight. Solidly medium-full in both strength and body this is not a cigar for the meek but should appeal to any enthusiast with a desire to taste the best in life. Exquisite when paired with hefty a pour of VSOP or even XO cognac, the Flor De Las Antillas Maduro is well prepared to take over the world even when all by itself. Come along for the ride.

Created by cigar master Manuel Quesada, the Fonseca Classic line of fine premium cigars is expertly handmade of long-filler leaf from the Cibao region of the Dominican Republic. The Fonseca Classic is a medium-strength cigar that is hand-rolled in the Dominican Republic. It features a light-brown Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper that covers a binder and filler made of tobacco from the Dominican Republic. (Shop other Fonseca Cigars ) The Fonseca Classic is a well-balanced cigar with notes of cedar and cream. If you want an easygoing yet elegant, mellow yet mouthwatering smoke, fill your humidor with the Fonseca brand of premium handmade cigars.

Fonseca has an image problem, they are known for making amazing mild cigars. Doesn't sound like too much of a problem right? Well it is when you are trying to build your market into more robust flavors but too many smokers shrug you off as the mild cigar company. When Fonseca released the Cubano Limitado, fans of the brand thought that Fonseca went too far in the opposite direction. Now with the release of the Cubano Exclusivo, they have found a happy medium. (Shop other Fonseca Cigars ) The Fonseca Cubano Exclusivo is a wonderful blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan filler tobaccos bound in a Dominican leaf and wrapped in a smooth Dominican Havana Vuelta Arriba wrapper. This cigar starts off firmly as a medium bodied smoke, but inches just slightly higher the more you smoke. Notes of the earth, wood, and pepper greet you and play off each other throughout the entire cigar. The final third brings more pepper to the forefront and downplays the other complexities but never drowns them out. If you have disregarded Fonseca before because you thought they were too mild a smoke for you, this is the cigar to try. Much more evenly flavored and bodied than anything from the fabled brand's past, the Cubano Exclusivo is a perfect medium-bodied stick.

More known for their milder cigars, Fonseca has created a medium-to-full-bodied masterpiece with their Cubano Limitado. Have you always wanted to smoke a Cuban cigar but keep letting those pesky customs laws get in your way? The Fonseca Cubano Limitado is about as close as you're going to get. Blended by the legend of the industry, Manuel Quesada, a filler of fantastic leaf from the Dominican Republic, a binder of strong Nicaraguan Ligero, and a beautiful dark and oily Honduran Habano wrapper perfectly mesh to give this cigar just the right amount of power and flavor. (Shop other Fonseca Cigars ) A minimalistic band of black and gold truly makes the complex flavors that await a hidden gem ready to be unearthed. The smooth, oily wrapper with hardly a vein to be seen is the first hint at the quality found beneath. First light brings on a spiciness which quickly gives way to a creamy cedar flavor. The aroma on the Fonseca Cubano Limitado is just as enticing as the flavors. Almost perfect construction, we found a slightly tight draw for the first few puffs, but that quickly opened up to a fantastic smoke. While there is some debate on whether this cigar is medium or full on the strength scale, we found it closer to the medium end. Fonseca's Cubano Limitado may be the closest you will get to tasting something similar to a cigar from that island south of Miami. Flavor, just enough power, and near perfect construction is what you can expect from the master behind this fantastic stogie, and it is exactly what you will get. The smoky cedar qualities of this cigar meshed perfectly with a nice sweet barbeque sauce, and is perfect for gatherings around the grill.

My Father Cigars is one of the most dominant giants of the cigar industry, so when they acquired the rights to Fonseca back in 2019, it was nothing short of a big deal, to say the least. Not only did the renowned Garcia family bring new life to the brand, so to speak, but they now had a new name in the company’s portfolio to expand on, and that they did. Behold, Fonseca Mexico Edition! Also known as Edition MX, this line extension puts Mexico in the spotlight by combining a gorgeous Mexican San Andres wrapper leaf with the all-Nicaraguan filler and binder blend that put My Father Fonseca at the top of the charts to begin with. Made at the world-famous My Father factory in Nicaragua, this all-new Fonseca brand has taken off, earning multiple 90 ratings in Cigar Aficionado and becoming a fixture in millions of humidors worldwide. A beautiful cedar chest decorated with both My Father and Fonseca logos houses the beautiful, handcrafted cigars, each vitola wearing 2 bands, the secondary designating the MX Edition. Built for maximum performance, this blend offers a smooth and productive draw that leaves nothing to be desired. White pepper is the opening flavor, and there is no shortage of it. A storm of spicy white pepper bombards the palate before the flavor profile opens up to a colorful array of savory spices wrapped around a dark, earthy core. Hints of coffee and cocoa dance around the outside of the flavor profile, and the finish is sweet, spicy, and smoky. Full-bodied to the max and balanced with precision, My Father Fonseca Mexico Edition is certainly a cigar that demonstrates what a classic Garcia family cigar should be. Fonseco Mexico Edition is made for the experienced. Newbies should look elsewhere. It takes a well-seasoned palate to be able to enjoy all the beautiful attributes that make this cigar as special as it is. Full-bodied and dark, this stick pairs well with dark beer, coffee, or dark rum. It compares to such full-bodied San Andres cigars as La Historia by EP Carrillo or Trinidad Espiritu Series No. 3 , so if you enjoy either, this might be your next big purchase! My Father Cigars took Fonseca to an entirely new level, and Fonseca Mexico Edition is a level that you simply have to experience to understand.

Foundation Cigars may not be the most talked about name in the business, but over the years the brand has more than proven itself to be connoisseur-worthy and then some. Aksum Claro is a re-branded blend that was previously offered by Foundation as Metapa Claro, and to this day it remains one of the company’s most sought-after brands. Made in Nicaragua by none other than AJ Fernandez, Aksum Claro pays homage to the history of the Aksumite Kingdom, a civilization of the ancient world located near modern-day Ethiopia. Legend has it that in ancient times, the Ark of the Covenant was brought to Aksum by Menelik the First, the supposed son of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. Local lore tells that the Ark remains there to this day, where it is guarded day and night by a single priest. Representing a blend of rich flavors and artisanal expertise, Aksum Claro couldn’t be a better fit to allude to such a story. As for the blend, the filler is from Nicaragua, the binder is Connecticut Broadleaf, and the wrapper is a gorgeous Sumatra Claro leaf grown in the volcanic soil of Ecuador. Though brand owner Nicholas Melillo’s blend may seem straightforward on paper, something magical happens when you set fire to it, and apparently the folks at Cigar Aficionado wholeheartedly agree, as they were quick to give Aksum Claro multiple 90+ ratings, the best being a very respectable 93. The same year, this blend made it into the famed magazine’s Top 25 Cigars of the Year. A refined cedar chest topped with a black and gold lid houses the expertly rolled vitolas, each one wearing a single blue and red band including a portrait of Ras Makonnen, a 19th Century governor of the Aksumite Kingdom. The construction is incredible on each cigar, and the draw is always easy and productive. Spicy Nicaraguan pepper explodes like a bomb upon lighting, soon followed by a blast of espresso and nuts. Woody nuances decorate the outer bands of the flavor profile, while an earthy raw tobacco core binds everything together in beautiful harmony. The finish is spicy, with no shortage of white pepper on the tip of the tongue. All-in-all, Aksum Claro finishes as a complex and well-balanced medium-full-bodied cigar. Not for newbies, Aksum Claro is geared towards the experienced. A well-developed palate and no shortage of patience are required to be able to fully enjoy all the good things this stick has to offer. Paired with bourbon or dark rum, Aksum Claro makes a fine treat at the end of a busy work week, but it is equally enjoyable with a cup of your favorite coffee or espresso after dinner. Cigars such as New World Dorado or San Lotano come to mind when thinking about similar stature, so if you have enjoyed either AJ Fernandez specialty, odds are you’re going to like this one. This cigar may pay homage to a story about the most sacred treasure of all time, but if we are being honest, Aksum Claro is a treasure in and of itself.

Nicholas Melillo and his Foundation Cigars have been on somewhat of a rampage in recent years, steadily gaining momentum with each and every new and delicious blend. One such blend is Aksum Maduro , the AJ Fernandez-made masterpiece coming out of Nicaragua that has been raising the eyebrows of maduro fans across the globe. Named after the fabled Aksumite Kingdom, where, according to legend, the Ark of the Covenant is located, this rich and tasty blend is already esteemed as one of Melillo’s best, and for good reason! The unique blend consists of Nicaraguan fillers from the fertile regions of Jalapa and Esteli, a Connecticut Broadleaf binder, and a dark, oily Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper leaf. Heavily aged and fermented to exacting standards, all tobacco used in the production of this cigar is considered to be ultra-premium and is selected by AJ Fernandez himself. Not that this cigar needs any further accolades, but its rating history in Cigar Aficionado is nothing short of stellar, with its highest rating yet being a rock-solid 92 . Black and gold cedar chests house the intricately crafted vitolas, each one wearing a simple gold, red, and blue band. Box-pressed, seamlessly rolled, and sporting a pigtail cap, Aksum Maduro is every bit as beautiful as it is delicious. Cedar and red pepper open things up at first light, soon settling into a scrumptious array of nuts, cocoa, and molasses . All this is wrapped around a core of earthy tobacco flavor, and the finish is sweet and crisp. Medium-full-bodied, Aksum Maduro tells one beautiful story as it smokes. Made for experienced connoisseurs, Aksum Maduro is one of the most easily recognizable Foundation cigars.
