Its complex and refined flavor profile, its medium-full-bodied feel, and its expert construction make it a cigar lover’s dream-come-true. It pairs well with black coffee, dark beer, or port wine and is certainly enjoyable at any time of the day. Fans of dark Nicaraguan sticks such as Oliva Serie V or My Father will definitely come to enjoy the rich and spicy flavor profile this cigar has to offer. Whether you are looking for something new and hot or care to follow Nicholas Melillo on his inevitable journey to the top, Aksum Maduro is a cigar you won’t want to pass up.

Nicholas Melillo of Foundation Cigars has more than rocked the world of premium cigars with his Charter Oak lineup, a collection of top-shelf, AJ Fernandez-made masterpieces that are all hit and no miss. In recent years, however, he wanted something more for the brand, something “special,” so he once again collaborated with AJ Fernandez to create Charter Oak Pegnataro, also known as Charter Oak Especiales CT Shade Pegnataro. Released alongside a darker, more robust sister cigar known as Pasquale, this Pegnataro blend uses an Ecuadorian Connecticut Seed Shade wrapper leaf over a Nicaraguan filler and binder blend. Incredibly flavorful for a Connecticut-wrapped cigar, this blend certainly personifies what a “fancy” Connecticut cigar should be. According to Melillo, “The Charter Oak core line would have been the everyday cigar, and these new blends (Pegnataro and Pasquale) would be for the weekend or a special occasion.” Whatever occasion you happen to choose, this choice of cigar is right. Both Pegnataro and Pasquale are available in one size, a 5 ½” x 48 Corona Gorda , or “long robusto,” as some call it. Rustic wooden boxes contain the expertly crafted cigars, made in the world-famous Tabacalera AJ Fernandez in Nicaragua. Each stick wears a classic Charter Oak band, but in gold and navy blue, with the addition of “Pegnataro” beneath the branding. A pigtail cap adds character to the cigars’ rustically beautiful appearance, and the construction is second to none. Billowing clouds of smoke massage the palate with a burst of cedar on the opening. Notes of leather and hay begin to hint towards an earthy main note, and before long, Pegnataro becomes a creamy dose of Connecticut goodness, combined with an earthy core of Nicaraguan tobacco flavor. Hints of white pepper on the finish round things out, and overall, this blend finishes on the heavier end of mild-medium-bodied . Crafted for long-time connoisseurs of mild-medium-bodied cigars, Pegnataro is rich, flavorful, and impeccably balanced. Easy on the palate, this Connecticut-wrapped beauty pairs well with scotch, cognac, or your favorite white wine. It is part of what has become an entire genre on today’s market, Ecuadorian Connecticut flavor bombs, sharing a place with the likes of Oliva Connecticut Reserve and Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real . For an unforgettable top-tier Connecticut smoking experience, you owe it to yourself to try Charter Oak Especiales CT Shade Pegnataro and find out just how flavorful and satisfying a simple Connecticut cigar really can be.

You may not know much about the Foundation Cigar Company right now, but you're sure as heck going to want to find out after trying the phenomenal Charter Oak Connecticut Shade cigar. After setting out on his own from Drew Estate and then stunning the world with the El Gueguense, Foundation founder Nicholas Melillo decided to honor his home state of Connecticut with a rich and creamy medium-bodied smoke coated in the only tobacco that would suffice: a flawless and golden Connecticut Shade. Named after a legendary tree that stood for centuries in Hartford as an icon of freedom, these affordable sticks are comprised of lush Nicaraguan filler, a spicy binder from Sumatra, and the aforementioned glorious wrapper. Melillio has made perhaps the wisest of choices by having each and every Foundation Charter Oak Connecticut Shade constructed at Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua, one of the highest-quality cigar factories on the planet. This means you can expect a level of craftmanship and smoking enjoyment far beyond that found in most other budget stogies. In perfect compliment to the sunny hue of each vitola, the band is a simple black and white affair decorated with an image of its namesake monument. Thick smoke pours easily through the well-balanced longleaf at the core of each stick, at first ripe with dark chocolate and nutmeg before mellowing slightly with cedar and cream. Some toasted almond enters near the halfway mark, joined soon after by a flourish of spice to keep the palate in thrall all the way to the nub. Priced for everyday enjoyment, you'll still find a reason to mark special occasions with one of these delectable treats. Not just another one of the forgettable mild stogies that litter the tobacco landscape, a Foundation Charter Oak Connecticut Shade cigar will be sought out again and again for their smooth, delightful character. Grab yourself a handful or a box today and get to having a grand old time.

Foundation Cigars is a name that has really picked up momentum in recent years, and some would agree that Charter Oak Especiales Pasquale is one of their best releases to date. Named after Foundation founder Nicholas Melillo's grandfathers, this line pays homage to the two men that introduced him to cigars and inspired him to be who he is today. In addition to paying homage to Melillo's grandfathers, this series also commemorates the company's new office on a 300-acre farm in the middle of the Connecticut River Valley growing region. Made at the famed AJ Fernandez factory in Nicaragua, the Especiales line consists of two variants (one for each grandfather): Pregnataro, a medium-bodied stick draped in a golden Connecticut shade wrapper leaf, and the cigar in question, Pasquale, a bolder, richer, fuller-bodied cigar boasting a nearly black Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. The filler and binder blend is made up entirely of aged Nicaraguan tobacco. Both variants are available in one size, a 5 ½" x 48 robusto size that offers a beautiful take on the flavor that Melillo and company worked so hard to achieve. Packed in humble cedar chests of 12, each vitola wears a single band depicting the Charter Oak tree the brand was originally inspired by, representing Melillo's home state of Connecticut. Meticulously crafted to offer a soft and abundant draw and an even burn, Pasquale starts off by sending billowing clouds of thick smoke to greet the palate. The first flavors include what one would expect from a dark Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro cigar: cocoa, espresso, and spicy black pepper. A soft dark chocolate note seems to be the core of the flavor profile, and the whole package is spiked with accents of sweet brown sugar throughout. The finish is long and heavy, yet all-in-all, the medium-full-bodied flavor profile is delicately balanced. As Melillo said in a press release, "The Charter Oak core line would have been [his grandfathers'] everyday cigar, and these new blends (Charter Oak Especiales) would be for the weekend or a special occasion." Well said, and we can't help but agree. This pair of beauties is called "Especiales" for a reason, and we can wholeheartedly recommend either blend to be a great special occasion accompaniment. Pasquale pairs well with coffee or dark beer and is similar in stature to such other fuller-bodied maduro cigars as Oliva Serie G Maduro or San Lotano Maduro , so if either fits your fancy, why not give Pasquale a shot? Nicholas Melillo is known for adding special meaning to his cigars, and Charter Oak Especiales Pasquale not only serves to commemorate his beloved grandfathers, but to provide the cigar world with an amazing maduro cigar that never disappoints.

The Charter Oak series from Foundation Cigars has proven that an incredible cigar doesn’t have to cost an arm and a leg, and with both a Connecticut and Broadleaf option in the lineup, there was something for almost everyone. The cigar world rejoiced when Nicholas Melillo announced a third option: Charter Oak Habano . This blend bridges the gap, presenting a medium-bodied option with a classic flavor profile that will appeal to smokers of all experience levels. For the recipe, we have Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco finished with a golden brown Ecuadorian Habano wrapper leaf. Like its counterparts, Charter Oak Habano is expertly crafted at the renowned Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars in Nicaragua. So let’s put it all together, a premium cigar rolled at one of the finest factories on the planet, using top shelf tobacco and blended by AJ Fernandez, all for a price that rivals most “bargain” cigars? What if we said it has earned as high as a 92 rating in Cigar Aficionado as well? By this point, there is little need for more convincing that this is anything short of a stellar offering. Wooden dress boxes house the single-banded cigars, each one wearing a white and black band depicting the centuries-old tree from Hartford, Connecticut after which the blend is named. The roll is velvety smooth, and the wrapper has a light sheen from the natural oils. A clean cut reveals an easy draw, one that produces delightful volumes of silky, white smoke. Black pepper is the dominant opening note, soon joined by a heavy presence of nuts and cream. Earthy tobacco undertones hold the profile together, as hints of cedar and bakers’ spices add to the complexity. A sweet, smooth finish rounds things out, and this blend settles precisely in the middle of the spectrum, the very definition of a medium-bodied cigar. Suitable for all audiences, this fantastic option is as versatile as it is delicious. More experienced connoisseurs will appreciate the subtle complexities and the overall value, while beginners will enjoy the easy, satisfying medium body. Pair this one with your favorite bourbon or scotch or simply enjoy it alongside a cup of hot coffee for a simple, yet memorable experience. Fans of the original Charter Oak lines, including CT Shade and CT Broadleaf , will definitely want to try this one for comparative purposes. A top-notch premium cigar from one of the finest brands, made by one of the best in the business, all for an affordable price? We agree, it sounds too good to be true, but you have to try one to believe it. No doubt, Charter Oak Habano will change the way you think about wallet-friendly cigars.

Ten years ago, Nicholas Melillo founded Foundation Cigar Company with a simple mission: honor the traditions of premium cigar making while telling stories rooted in history, culture, and exceptional tobacco. In the years that followed, Foundation became one of the industry's most respected boutique manufacturers, producing acclaimed blends that seamlessly combine old-world craftsmanship with modern innovation. To commemorate this remarkable milestone, Melillo presents the Foundation 10 Year Aniversario Salomon , a limited-edition release that celebrates a decade of dedication, creativity, and uncompromising quality. This cigar earned an outstanding 91 rating from Cigar Aficionado , affirming Nicholas Melillo’s legacy of crafting top-tier, highly acclaimed releases. Handcrafted at the renowned AJ Fernandez factory in Nicaragua , this commemorative blend showcases some of the finest tobaccos Foundation has ever assembled. At its core lies a rich combination of premium Nicaraguan fillers from Estelí, Jalapa, and Condega, secured beneath a flavorful Brazilian Mata Fina binder. The finishing touch is a truly distinctive Connecticut Broadleaf and CT Havana Seed hybrid wrapper , cultivated in Connecticut's famed River Valley on the very farm that also serves as Foundation's corporate headquarters. The result is a cigar that pays tribute not only to the company's heritage, but also to the tobacco-growing traditions that helped shape Nicholas Melillo's career. Presented in an elegant 7" x 58 Salomon vitola, the cigar allows the blend to evolve gradually as the smoke progresses. The tapered foot delivers a focused, concentrated opening before the wider body fully reveals the blend's remarkable complexity. Thick, velvety clouds of smoke introduce rich notes of dark chocolate, espresso , and earthy tobacco , followed by layers of cedar, black pepper, and baking spice . As the cigar develops, subtle natural sweetness emerges, balancing the richer components and creating a smooth, refined finish that lingers long after the final draw. The presentation is every bit as meaningful as the blend itself. Inspired by Saint George and the Dragon, the commemorative artwork symbolizes courage, perseverance, and triumph, qualities that have defined Foundation Cigars since its inception. Produced in an extremely limited run of just 35,000 cigars , the Foundation 10 Year Aniversario Salomon is far more than a celebration of the company's past. It is a statement of everything Foundation has become and a fitting tribute to one of the most influential boutique cigar makers of the modern era. Whether you're a longtime Foundation devotee or discovering Nicholas Melillo's craftsmanship for the first time, this exceptional anniversary release is destined to become one of the crown jewels of your humidor.

Master Blender Nick Melillo has been around tobacco all his life, a charmed existence indeed culminating in the remarkable Charter Oak Connecticut Broadleaf cigar. Gifted with an innate taste for good longleaf, Melillo wasn't long out of school before finding himself at Drew Estate, where he would rise to VP. The desire to create his own brands necessitated a gracious departure and soon the Foundation Cigar Company was started in the same lush tobacco-growing region of Connecticut where Melillo grew up, which also happens to be the source of the magnificent Broadleaf wrapper that so gracefully covers the rich Nicaraguan filler at the core of each vitola. It is obvious that a lot of love went into the creation of the Charter Oak Connecticut Broadleaf, for each solidly-built cigar exudes a character that can't be accounted for simply by the quality of its construction. Or maybe it's just the heady aroma of sweet cocoa and ripe tobacco that wafts from the shimmering outer leaf. The foot is rolled closed, but the draw through an unlit stick is open enough to provide hints of cedar and dried fruit. Easily lit, this smoke factory of a stick opens semi-sweet with dark chocolate and earth atop more subtle flavors of citrus and hazelnut. Becoming somewhat peppery at the midpoint, this is also where coffee and a touch of caramel enter to keep the strength hovering just above the middle mark. The low price we have listed for these fine smokes is no typo, ladies and gentlemen. Designed as a bargain cigar from the get-go, the folks at Foundation have simply outdone themselves. A Charter Oak Connecticut Broadleaf cigar can rise to your most demanding occasion but serves just as well each day with a morning Cup o' Joe or two (maybe three) fingers of whiskey in the evening. Take advantage of this great deal before we all come to our senses.

When George Carnarvon, the Eighth Earl of Carnarvon, commissioned Foundation Cigar Company to make a cigar named after his famous English castle in Highclere, Hampshire, Highclere Castle Victorian was born. The project is actually a collaboration between Foundation and AJ Fernandez, who makes the cigars at his state-of-the-art factory in Nicaragua. The blend is comprised of Nicaraguan filler tobacco, a Brazilian Mata Fina binder, and a dark, oily Ecuadorian Habano wrapper leaf. Every bit as luxurious as the castle it's named after, Highclere Castle Victorian has earned a 93 rating from Cigar Aficionado and a spot on the Top 25 Cigars of 2020. Simple, yet fancy red and gold bands hug each expertly crafted vitola. A nearly seamless roll ensures an even burn, sharp ash, and an easy draw that produces plenty of silky white smoke. Black pepper is the first thing to hit the palate, bringing about the familiar Nicaraguan spice that AJ Fernandez is so well-known for. Shortly thereafter, earthy tobacco flavor, cream, and cedar join the mix, with a sweet finish through the nose. Notes of chocolate, cinnamon, and red pepper are noticeable throughout the delightfully simple smoking experience, and by the end Highclere Castle Victorian finishes just above medium-bodied. Made with the discriminating aficionado in mind, Highclere Castle Victorian is an upper tier cigar aimed at more experienced smokers. The profile is quite simple, yet the subtle complexities contained therein call for a well-seasoned palate for true enjoyment. This blend pairs well with bourbon, red wine, or even coffee, and is appropriate for any time of the day. Fans of AJ Fernandez sticks such as New World or Bellas Artes will likely thoroughly enjoy the blend in question. For some of us, a good cigar gives us the taste of luxury we need to enjoy the fruits of our labor. That taste of luxury gets a whole lot better with Highclere Castle Victorian, so don't hesitate to try one the next time you are in search of something new!

Headlining the award-winning Highclere Castle series from Foundation Cigars, Highclere Castle Edwardian is a refined cigar made with the sophisticated connoisseur in mind. The Highclere Castle project is a collaboration between brand owner Nick Melillo and the Earl of Carnarvon, paying homage to the cigars enjoyed by British Nobility in the early 20 th Century. Made at the AJ Fernandez’s famed factory in Esteli, Nicaragua, this meticulously crafted blend contains a spicy Brazilian Mata Fina binder along with a filler combination of hybrid Nicaraguan Corojo and Criollo leaves known as Nicadan, cultivated in Jalapa and Ometepe. The wrapper is a Connecticut shade leaf grown in the volcanic soil of Ecuador. Simple, yet intriguing, this mix works together to create a 92-rated masterpiece that is sure to leave a lasting impression. Blue and gold cedar chests, white and gold bands, and expert craftsmanship combine to make a product that looks every bit as good as it tastes. A smooth draw produces dense ribbons of silky smoke, while a razor-sharp burn and firm ash provide a classic experience every time. An initial greeting of spicy white pepper soon settles into a creamy, flavorful mixture of cinnamon, citrus, and earth , all culminating into a core of classic raw tobacco flavor. The finish is creamy and crisp, and altogether Edwardian finishes as a solid medium-bodied cigar. Made for the most demanding aficionados, Highclere Castle Edwardian is a top-tier cigar that offers a complex medium-bodied smoking experience like the premium cigars of old. Pair this one with your favorite scotch, white wine, or hot tea and be sure to set aside plenty of time to take in all the subtle nuances this blend has to offer. Fans of Foundation’s other Connecticut highlights such as Charter Oak Connecticut or The Tabernacle No. 142 are surely going to want to give this one a try. If you’re in the market for something special, try a Highclere Castle Edwardian and smoke like the nobility, and don’t hesitate to enjoy every second of it.

Olmec Claro by Foundation Cigars demonstrates the true beauty of Mexican tobacco while paying homage to one of the most ancient civilizations of North America. Named after the natives indigenous to the area where today’s Mexican tobacco is grown and harvested, Nicholas Melillo’s Olmec series is available in 2 variations: Maduro and Claro. This Claro version has a lighter wrapper leaf and offers a more crisp and light-hearted smoking experience. Like all Foundation cigars, Olmec Claro is made by the skilled hands at AJ Fernandez’s factory in Nicaragua. The blend consists of select 3 year-aged Nicaraguan filler leaves from Esteli and Jalapa, a Nicaraguan binder, and a caramel brown Mexican San Andres Claro leaf. Sounds tasty, right? The folks at Cigar Aficionado certainly seemed to think so, as in 2023 Olmec Claro earned a stellar 93 rating, along with a spot on the magazine’s prestigious Top 25 Cigars of the Year list. Handsome cedar chests house the single banded vitolas, each dressed in black, yellow, and gold. Construction leaves absolutely nothing to be desired, as each mildly pressed oily beauty is rolled precisely to offer an easy, productive draw every single time. Cocoa and pepper open things up, followed up by a one-two punch of cedar and raw tobacco . Sweet bakers’ spices decorate the edges of the flavor profile, and a definitive ginger note is detectable on the crisp, clean finish. Medium-full-bodied and delicately complex, Olmec Claro is a cigar built for the most discriminating connoisseurs. Made for the experienced, Olmec Claro follows suit behind its Foundation Cigars brothers and sisters. It is uncannily refined, astonishingly complex, and offers a satisfying experience guaranteed to please any palate that yearns for a luxuriously delicious smoking experience. Pair it with your favorite bourbon, scotch, or medium-bodied beer for a relaxing and unforgettable smoking session that will have you coming back for more every time. Fans of cigars such as New World Decenio or San Lotano will definitely appreciate the AJ Fernandez DNA incorporated into the blend. Take a journey into the world of how premium cigars should be. Try an Omec Claro and celebrate the heritage of Mexican Tobacco the Foundation way.

Foundation Cigars and AJ Fernandez have teamed up once again, and this time the masterpiece is of the maduro variety! Behold, Olmec Maduro ! This stick is part 2 of a 2-cigar series which pays homage to the land of the ancient Olmecs, now modern-day Veracruz, Tabasco, and San Andres Tuxtla. In other words, it is the part of Mexico that is known for growing some of the best maduro tobacco on the planet. Olmec Maduro is handmade at the AJ Fernandez factory in Nicaragua using only the finest Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco. This extensively aged package is then finished with a dark, oily, and absolutely gorgeous San Andres Maduro wrapper leaf grown in the very region the brand honors. Spicy, flavorful, and rich, Olmec Maduro has garnered quite a bit of admiration, not to mention multiple 90+ ratings in Cigar Aficionado , the highest being a very respectable 94 . Housed in a beautiful cedar chest, Olmec Maduro wears a yellow and black band reminiscent of a classic Cuban cigar at first glance. The construction leaves nothing to be desired, as this cigar is produced at one of the world’s foremost cigar factories, and AJ Fernandez leaves no detail overlooked. An easy draw produces thick bursts of smoke, which at first puff offer astounding flavors of spice and coffee. Cedar, cocoa, and cinnamon are quick to join the party, and as the cigar progresses, the rich, earthy core makes its way to the forefront. A black cherry finish ties the package together, and overall Olmec Maduro finishes strong as a full-bodied cigar . Well-balanced, complex, and packed with flavor, Olmec Maduro is a connoisseur’s dream-come-true. This especially applies to cigar fanatics that tend to lean towards maduro cigars, as we all know there is just something special about a good San Andres Maduro. Pair this flavor bomb with black coffee or tawny port for a truly invigorating experience, and feel free to see how it stacks up to such other top San Andres sticks as La Historia or The Wise Man Maduro . Whether a long-time supporter of AJ Fernandez, a fan of today’s Foundation Cigars, or just someone that appreciates a good, solid maduro stick, Olmec Maduro by Foundation Cigars is a gem that deserves a spot in your humidor.

The Tabernacle is a cigar made for aficionados, by an aficionado. The second line in the Foundation series, The Tabernacle brand encompasses themes from the Bible, King Solomon, and the Ark of the Covenant. The Foundation brand is owned and operated by former Head of Production at La Gran Fabrica Drew Estate, Nicholas Melillo. After spending over a decade in Nicaragua while working for Jonathan Drew and company, Melillo built quite the reputation for himself, becoming known as somewhat of a master at blending hearty Nicaraguan tobaccos and producing amazing blends, some of his more notable accolades being none other than Liga Privada No. 9, UF-13, T52, and of course, Nica Rustica. After parting ways with Drew Estate, Melillo began the Foundation brand, his first release, El Gueguense, garnering unusually high ratings and even a spot on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 list. Then came The Tabernacle, a sort of collaboration with industry rock star AJ Fernandez. Made down in Nicaragua at the famed Tabacalera Fernandez; The Tabernacle is rolled using some of the finest tobacco in the world, a good bit of it coming from AJ's personal farm, La Soledad. Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers, a Mexican San Andres binder, and a dark, toothy Connecticut broadleaf Maduro wrapper make this cigar as flavorful as it is beautiful. The Tabernacle blend has received a multiple prestigious 90 ratings from Cigar Aficionado magazine. Rolled in typical AJ Fernandez fashion, The Tabernacle is precisely constructed to offer a smooth, easy draw and a plethora of thick, flavorful smoke. Beginning with a blast of white pepper, The Tabernacle quickly transitions to a smooth, pleasant, classic Maduro flavor profile. Chocolate, espresso, nuts, and spice massage the palate as a raw tobacco presence in the background holds it all together. A sweet finish and a smooth retrohale further add to the depth and complexity of the blend. Overall, The Tabernacle is an amazing display of blending prowess and tobacco expertise. It takes Maduro into a whole new dimension. As one may conclude, Foundation The Tabernacle, is not a beginners' cigar, like the other masterpieces on Melillo's resume. It is an ultra-premium blend made with discriminating palates in mind. In other words, only true connoisseurs need to apply. Sitting at the high end of medium-to-full, The Tabernacle pairs wonderfully with coffee, port wine, or dark beer, and is best enjoyed after a good meal. Similar sticks may include Liga Privada No. 9 and Nica Rustica, both of which Nicholas Melillo had a huge part in producing. When asked about the name of this stick, Melillo described how when he was growing up in Connecticut; he began smoking cigars with his grandfather. He considered their time spent smoking together to be sacred, and his humidor became his "tabernacle." Quite the story, really, and quite a cigar as well. Nicholas Melillo has nothing to prove. He has already had a hand in some of the most famous cigars in history. However, now it is his time to truly shine, and Foundation The Tabernacle is doubtless destined to be something huge.

Foundation Cigars is best known for their upper-tier creations geared toward serious aficionados, but they have stepped outside of the box to offer something edgy, fun, and downright delicious: The Upsetters Maduro . For those who don’t know, the Upsetters is a series of Nicaraguan-made cigars that pay homage to the rich history of Jamaica. In addition to a premium blend of Nicaraguan filler and binder tobacco, each and every Upsetters cigar contains a dose of Jamaican Cow Tongue leaf, tobacco native to Jamaica and grown in the very region where the indigenous Arawak people grew tobacco centuries ago. The Upsetters series contains 8 sizes, each sporting a different wrapper leaf. This Maduro variant is cloaked with a dark and oily Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro wrapper, and like all cigars in the series, the tobacco has undergone “Caribbean Atmospheric Herbal Fusion” to give it a uniquely beautiful, infused aroma and flavor profile. Black boxes and bands with rainbow accents and logos are the common denominators across the board with the Upsetters series. To make it easier, however, each cigar wears a secondary band denoting both the size and title. The pre-light aroma may seem a bit overwhelming at first, something like stepping into a herb shop or tropical greenhouse but relaxing. This intense bouquet is only on the surface. The easy draw provides plenty of smoke on every puff, and just a hint of the pre-light aroma is detectable amid the rich maduro flavor profile. Notes of rich tobacco, coffee, and cocoa dazzle the taste buds as peppery spice lingers in the background. Medium-bodied, the Upsetters Maduro really shines as the go-to Maduro of the bunch. Suitable for all audiences, the Upsetters Maduro tells a story with its flavor profile. Unlike other infused cigars, the surface aroma doesn’t translate much into the actual flavor of the smoke, making it a great choice for anyone who may have given infused cigars a try but quickly ran the other way, so to speak. It pairs well with black coffee, dark beer, or dark rum, and is a great choice for any fan of mildly-infused cigars such as Larutan or Isla Del Sol . The motto of the brand is “Dare to be different.” It goes without saying that if you do in fact dare to be different and grab an Upsetters Maduro, your taste buds will thank you!

It’s been over a decade since Nicholas Melillo’s Foundation Cigar Company debuted with El Gueguense and rocked the world of premium cigars. Now, more blends are being introduced year by year, and El Gueguense is now represented in its English translation: The Wise Man. 2024 marked the release of The Wise Man Corojo cigar , a Nicaraguan-made masterpiece that seriously spiced things up for the brand (literally). Formerly made by Aganorsa Leaf, The Wise Man, along with all Foundation cigars, are now produced at the world famous My Father factory in Nicaragua, with blending and production being overseen by none other than Don Pepin and Jaime Garcia. That being said, it’s not surprising that Foundation now offers a top-notch Corojo stick, and a darned good one at that. In fact, this package is a Nicaraguan puro, meaning all tobacco used for the blend comes from the fertile soil of Nicaragua—wrapper, filler, and binder. Every leaf is grown in Nicaragua’s finest growing regions of Esteli, Jalapa, and Condega, and the wrapper leaf is a gorgeous red-hued Nicaraguan Corojo, one of Don Pepin’s favorites. Not that such a stellar concoction needs any additional selling points, but The Wise Man Corojo has earned multiple high ratings in Cigar Aficionado, including a very respectable 91 in early 2025 . The cedar chest housing the cigars is exquisite, adorned in striking blue and gold. Matching blue and gold bands accented with a green cross distinguish the Corojo variant of the brand, while the construction leaves absolutely nothing to be desired. The easy draw produces thick, billowing clouds of white smoke that initially hit the palate with a blast of bold, spicy Pepin pepper . The intensity lingers for a while before giving way to a refined medley of coffee, tea leaves, and baker’s spices — flavors often found in ultra-premium Nicaraguan Corojo cigars. A subtle touch of cocoa on the finish rounds out the experience, and when the smoke clears, The Wise Man Corojo lands just a notch below full-bodied. Made for the most experienced connoisseurs, The Wise Man Corojo is alluring in every aspect, from its complex, classic Nicaraguan flavor profile to its stout body and rich, powerful undertones. It pairs beautifully with bourbon, dark rum, or full-bodied beer, but can accompany a hot cup of black coffee just as well. Similar in stature to Don Pepin Blue or the celebrated Flor de Las Antillas , this spicy Corojo creation is sure to satisfy even the pickiest cigar freak. Do you consider yourself to be wise? If so, your best bet at this point is to try a Wise Man Corojo and experience what the new, improved Foundation Cigar Company has to offer.

When Nicholas Melillo left his long-time position with Drew Estate and started Foundation Cigars , his first release made massive waves throughout the industry. That release was El Gueguense , an ultra-premium cigar named after a Nicaraguan folk dance which translates literally to “The Wise Man.” Soon after, those waves became tsunamis with the introduction of The Wise Man Maduro, the dark, sultry follow-up to the original. In addition, blending and production has now shifted to the watchful eyes of Jaime and Don Pepin Garcia, two of the biggest names in the business. Now rolled by the skilled hands at the world famous My Father factory in Nicaragua, The Wise Man Maduro begins with an all-Nicaraguan filler and binder blend, including leaves from all 3 major growing regions: Jalapa, Condega, and Esteli. This package is then topped off with a gorgeous Mexican San Andres Maduro wrapper leaf, something long-awaited from someone with a nickname like “Chief of the Broadleaf.” Was the final product as good as everyone was expecting? Well, a stellar 95 rating in Cigar Aficionado and a top spot on the famed magazine’s Top 25 Cigars of 2018 list pretty much says it all! Newly done bands of maroon and gold adorn each hand-crafted masterpiece, each cigar oozing with natural oils and glistening in the light. As one would expect from a cigar rolled under the supervision of the Garcias, construction is phenomenal, and the draw is easy and productive every time. White pepper mixed with dark chocolate opens things up, and there is a hint of cayenne on the tip of the tongue. A dark, earthy core of rich, spicy tobacco is at the center of the show, and notes of caramel, toast, and cinnamon dance around the outside of the flavor profile. The finish is clean and sweet, and overall, The Wise Man Maduro finishes at medium-full-bodied, with no shortage of delicious complexity. Made for more experienced connoisseurs, The Wise Man Maduro is a more-than-worthy follow-up to its natural predecessor. Complex, velvety smooth, and medium-full-bodied, it is everything a discriminating cigar enthusiast could ask for. It pairs beautifully with coffee, port wine, or dark rum and is certainly suitable for use as a celebratory cigar. Fans of the original El Gueguense should be quite pleased at the flavorful differences this cigar brings to the table. Would it be foolish to pass up a cigar this good? Well, we will let the name of the stick answer that question. Make a wise decision: Try The Wise Man Maduro today and experience one of Nicaragua’s most luxurious offerings.

Fratello Oro is the first cigar in the Fratello portfolio to be produced outside the Joya De Nicaragua factory. This time, Fratello founder Omar de Frias went across the map to the Dominican Republic, assigning the task to La Aurora, the country's oldest cigar factory. Not only is Oro the first Dominican-made Fratello, but it is also the first to use a Connecticut shade wrapper, in this case a golden Ecuadorian variety. This, combined with a Cameroon binder and a filler blend from Nicaragua, Colombia, and the Dominican Republic, makes for an amazing mild-medium-bodied smoking experience that even seasoned connoisseurs can appreciate. For a premium Connecticut-wrapped stick, Fratello Oro is rather rustic in appearance. Despite the glistening gold bands, the classic Cuban style roll and textured wrapper leaf add a unique amount of old school character. Speaking of that roll, it is just right, lending to a great draw and a solid ash to boot. As for flavor characteristics, Oro is all that one would expect from a designer Connecticut cigar: creamy, earthy, and nutty. A bit of cedar adds something extra to the blend, as well as hints of spicy white pepper and a tangy citrus note in the background. A bread note is noticeable on the retrohale, as well as just a bit of sweetness on the tip of the tongue. Beginning as a very mild cigar, this stick in particular builds just enough intensity throughout the smoke to bring it into medium-bodied territory by the closing puffs. Like most mild-medium-bodied cigars, Fratello Oro is most definitely suitable for beginners, though its subtle complexities, velvety smoothness, and all the other bells and whistles included in this price point will likely go to waste on an inexperienced palate. Of course, the usual white wine, light beer, and even Champagne all go well with Oro, but oddly enough the notes in the flavor profile actually pair beautifully with orange juice, making it a great breakfast cigar. If you have come to enjoy such Ecuadorian Connecticut beauties as Montecristo Classic or Romeo y Julieta Reserva Real , perhaps it would be worth your while to check out Fratello Oro and compare it. "Oro" is Spanish for "gold," and this golden beauty is most definitely a fantastic choice for any lover of fine mild-medium cigars.
Creamy , Rich , Cocoa Available. Learn about Gispert Intenso Cigars. Check out reviews and get details on Intenso

The end result of a collaboration of giants, the Gispert Intenso cigar takes taste, strength, and pure smoking enjoyment to the next level. It's an old brand name to be sure, one not everyone will know, but rest assured that a Gispert frontmark has always represented succulent, satisfying flavor. Now, bringing his particular brand of magic to the table, the incomparable AJ Fernandez worked side by side with the masters of tobacco at Grupo de Maestros to create a new and potent blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan longleaf tobaccos, far greater than the sum of its parts. The addition of a perfectly aged and fermented Ecuadorian Connecticut Broadleaf as the wrapper seals the deal to make the Gispert Intenso a powerful delight. Carrying a light box-press, each solidly crafted Gispert Intenso vitola is a toothy and dark brown love note written by skilled hands to your eyes, nose, and palate. Heavy and solid, the oily barrel of the cigar wafts a mouth-watering aroma of cedar and chocolate even before being lit, but it is after a flame is applied that this cigar really demands your attention. Fernandez has taken the seemingly commonplace individual longleaf tobaccos within and married them in such a way as to create a complex and rich flavor profile loaded with oak, bittersweet cocoa, black pepper, leather, and cream. Take this full-bodied treat for a spin and give your taste buds the kick they are craving. A Gispert Intenso is not so overpowering that less experienced smokers need to shy away, so don't be afraid to load up your cart. At the same time, this cigar offers true aficionados much to explore through wise beverage pairings and contemplative puffing. The best part is, they're priced so affordable to where anybody who wants to enjoy them can. Want in on the action? Get yours now.

God of Fire 2014 Serie Aniversario cigars are finally here and they are true world-class smokes that should be on every aficionado's bucket list. Originally announced as a 2012 release to celebrate Prometheus International's 20th year, some unfortunate delays have morphed them into signifying their God of Fire brand's 10 year anniversary. Not that it matters why they're here or what year is on the label because holy moly are these some delicious sticks. Crafted by the incomparable Fuente family, each Dominican-filled treasure is coated with a savory Ecuadorian wrapper of such exquisite quality you might think you've died and gone to heaven. (Shop other God of Fire Cigars ) There's just something immediately sophisticated about a figurado cigar, that classic and difficult to roll shape given to all three God of Fire 2014 vitolas. Redolently earthy in aroma and with cocoa and mesquite cold-draw flavors, it's almost possible to overlook the impressive design and construction that went into each stick, but there is nothing wrong with spending time in quiet appreciation before lighting that flame. Anticipation builds as the narrow foot gives hints of sweet vanilla and white pepper, but once the main body of the cigar starts to slowly smolder these are joined in full force by creamy leather, espresso, and oak backed by an amazing floral aroma. The second half adds toasted peanuts, a meaty char and a whisper of mint through the nose before reaching a spicy finish that is a religious experience all in itself. Despite the complexity of flavor to be found, expect an eventful medium bodied experience perfect for acolytes and masters alike. The God of Fire 2014 Serie Aniversario is a special occasion cigar that you will find no excuse not to smoke, so take advantage of our amazing prices and join this cult of personality today.

Gran Habano 3 SLS Robusto cigars are cigars that have a fascinating and decorated history behind them. Made down in Honduras by the George Rico and his famed Gran Habano Cigar Company, 3 SLS is a hearty blend of Costa Rican and long Nicaraguan fillers wrapped with a Nicaraguan binder and finished with a dark, oily Habano wrapper leaf. Formerly known as "3 Siglos," 3 SLS won many honors, the best of which was in 2007 when it was named one Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 cigars with a stellar rating of 92. Once highly regarded as a super premium, 3 SLS is now discontinued by the Gran Habano Company and is available at absolutely killer prices. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) Gran Habano 3 SLS is constructed to the famous Gran Habano standards, with a firm draw that produces clouds of thick white smoke. From the very first puff, 3 SLS is rich, powerful, and full-bodied, opening with a blast of cedar and continuing with cinnamon, cocoa, and earthy goodness. A woody sweetness on the finish makes 3 SLS a well-rounded experience, finishing off a flavor bouquet that is both complex and bold at the same time. Gran Habano 3 SLS was designed initially as a cigar for connoisseurs, sitting at the top of the Gran Habano portfolio. However, at today's prices, it is readily available and affordable to just about everyone. Seasoned smokers will appreciate the rich complexity, while those who do not quite have a finely-tuned palate will get a rush from the full-bodied power the stick offers. 3SLS pairs well with dark beer and coffee, and it is a good chance that if you are a fan of Oliva Serie V or Casa Magna , you will probably fall in love with it at the first puff. Get it while it is still available, as Gran Habano 3 Robusto will doubtless go down in history as one of the great cigars made by George Rico and company.

An early example from the 2010's Double Maduro frenzy, the Gran Habano Azteca Gran Robusto stands the test of time. Following on the success of their Gran Habano #1, #3, and #5 blends, the father and son team of Guillermo and George Rico crafted their first Maduro smoke with an eye on the future even as they held firm to the Rico family's connection with tobacco that stretches back four generations. Starting with a succulent blend of Nicaraguan, Habano, and Panamanian longleaf filler, they fed the growing appetite for stogies rolled with paired Maduros with the fateful decision to use juicy, well-fermented Mexican San Andres leaves, a regional variety destined to become near-dominant in today's dark cigar world, as both wrapper and binder. The oils that glint off of the sleek umber brown Maduro wrapper should please Tonatiuh the Sun God as he gazes from the stick's golden band upon the fortunate enthusiast holding a Gran Habano Azteca Gran Robusto. A pungent aroma foretells the pre-light flavor of loamy earth, which in turn prepares the palate for thick clouds of smoke full of espresso and rye toast. A creamy caramel sweetness can be detected from the midpoint all the way to the finish alongside more robust flavors of oak, chocolate covered almonds, and leather.

George Rico has some interesting ideas when it comes to boutique cigars, but we'll let him do what he does as long as he keeps releasing gems such as the Gran Habano S.T.K. Black Dahlia. Much of the time, so-called 'boutique' stogies come from small, often obscure companies and while they can sometimes be fantastic sticks, they don't always live up to the hype. Then there's the other common usage for the term, of which Rico's various 'Gran Habano S.T.K.' frontmarks are a part: Cigars from known makers that for valid reasons are limited or short run batches. The S.T.K. Black Dahlia is a regular, albeit small, production run containing Nicaraguan Cubita and Habano, Colombian, and Costa Rican longleaf filler beneath dual Habano binders and a creamy shade-grown Corojo wrapper, all from Nicaragua. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) The multi-pedaled and ebony-hued namesake flower that adorns the otherwise white and gold band just below an embossed S.T.K. (Stay True Kid) label is the only thing actually black about a Gran Habano S.T.K. Black Dahlia, the solid barrel of which is simply a rich light-brown color. After inhaling the crisp and sweet tobacco aroma that wafts from the vitola, the wise enthusiast will quickly move to the lighting stage to release the first bursts of black pepper, cracked wheat, and sweet cream delivered by a near-overwhelming amount of thick smoke. Easily medium-full from the beginning, this savory cigar stays cool burning as the flavors of espresso, cedar, almond paste, gingerbread, raisins, and orange peel all take turns wowing the tastebuds. One of the best things about the widening of the boutique description is when it merges new tastes with quality and affordability, all traits the Gran Habano S.T.K. Black Dahlia carries in spades. Dig yourself out of that cigar rut you've somehow found yourself in and try one or more of these quality stogies before we run out. Not that we will, but it can happen.

Gran Habano #1 Connecticut cigars are the smoothest, mildest, most easy-to-smoke blend from the otherwise high-powered Gran Habano brand. Handmade in Danli, Honduras, these beauties include a concoction of medium-bodied Nicaraguan filler and binder tobaccos and a golden brown Ecuador Connecticut wrapper leaf. Like all Gran Habano blends, the #1 Connecticut is the product of brand owners Guillermo and George Rico. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) This top-rated blend, which earned an impressive 90 rating from Cigar Aficionado , showcases the expert craftsmanship and consistency that have made Gran Habano a respected name among cigar enthusiasts worldwide. These cigars are well-made with an easy draw. The smoke is thick and gray, coating the palate with creamy, earthy flavors including hints of nuts and vanilla. The finish is short and clean, leaving behind a tiny hint of grass. They are pleasant, smooth, and well-balanced. Medium-bodied. The #1 Connecticut cigars are a terrific, wallet-friendly choice for beginners and intermediate smokers. They are wonderful for any time of day and pair well with white wine. They are comparable to Oliva Connecticut Reserve and Camacho Connecticut, two other fine Connecticut-wrapped medium-strength sticks. Take it easy, relax, and grab a Gran Habano #1 Connecticut cigar today!

Gran Habano Corojo Maduro #5 is a cigar with a long name, a long history, and most likely a long future ahead of it. Made down in Honduras under the supervision of George Rico, Corojo Maduro #5 is the maduro-clad sister cigar of the celebrated classic Corojo #5 that seems to have been around forever. The Gran Habano name is synonymous with value, quality, and versatility, and appeals to cigar smokers of every stature. For most, the maduro version of Corojo #5 is a welcomed addition to the lineup. It consists of a filler and binder blend of Nicaraguan and Costa Rican tobaccos married with a dark, toothy Nicaraguan Corojo Maduro leaf. The result is a unique cigar that's sure to leave a big impression. Modern, Cuban-style packaging and bands give Corojo Maduro #5 a high-end feel, ideally complementing the superb construction and gorgeous Nicaraguan Corojo Maduro wrapper leaves. A firm draw delivers ample amounts of heavy white smoke, coating the palate with a spicy array of nutty, earthy flavors. Coffee, black pepper, and chocolate are the main notes , along with a hint of cherry and floral flavor on the retrohale. A spicy, clean finish ties the bold, rich package together very nicely. Gran Habano Corojo Maduro #5 is very full-bodied. There's no way around it. The original Corojo #5 was full-bodied, to begin with, but this one takes it a step further. Experienced cigar connoisseurs should be the main crowd for this one. It pairs beautifully with tawny port and dark rum and can even be enjoyed with coffee. Corojo Maduro #5 can be compared to Camacho Triple Maduro and Partagas Black, other full-bodied maduro cigars that, like this one, just seem to be put together beautifully. If you love maduros, if you love full-bodied cigars, if you love value, and if you love quality, look no further than Gran Habano Corojo Maduro #5. We promise you won't regret it. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars )

When Guillermo Rico and George A. Rico had a falling out, George created a new brand G.A.R. Cigars. While the father and son are back together again, G.A.R. continues to be made to this day. The G.A.R. White is the original blend, packaged in unique white boxes of twenty cigars featuring simplistic white foot bands. G.A.R. White is offered in four box-pressed sizes from the Rico's Honduran factory: Gran Consul (4 3/4" x 60); Corona Gorda (6" x 46), Rico Grande (6" x 54) and Robusto Grande (5 1/2" x 52) with an Ecuadorian Corojo wrapper over an Ecuadorian binder and Nicaraguan fillers. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) For fans of Corojo, you'll notice cedar, pepper and leather. However, it's joined by sweetness, a more generic woodsiness, and a bit of earth. While George Rico claims this is a full cigar, it's more medium-full in body, medium in strength, and medium-full in flavor. Don't shy away from the dark wrapper; this is a great cigar to pair with coffee or enjoy through out any part of the day. For those that have enjoyed Gran Habanos over the years, G.A.R. might be a step up in strength, but the quality remains the same.

After slowly working their way into our hearts and minds by releasing wave after wave of affordable yet beloved smokes, the cigar fanatics at Gran Habano are coming to take over our humidors with the 93-rated Gran Habano La Conquista. Flush with expertly fermented and finely aged longleaf perfect for creating a medium-to-full bodied experience, these sturdy sticks will delight the palate in myriad ways. Complexity is assured through the inspired inclusion of Colombian, Costa Rican, and Nicaraguan tobaccos as the action-packed filler nearly bursting from beneath the leathery and slick Nicaraguan Corojo binder and wrapper. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) Thickly bunched yet able to provide smooth airflow during all draws both before and after lighting, the core of each crafted vitola tempts the nose with spice and dry cocoa while the golden and oily outer Corojo sets the lips to tingle ever so slightly. If you discover the initial flavor of a lit Gran Habano La Conquista is overwhelmingly of charred wood then you didn't remove the cedar sleeve which protects the lower bout of each stick, a mistake you only make once. The actual profile, while certainly containing warm bursts of cedar, is heavily laden with black pepper, French roast coffee, molasses, peat, whipping cream, and cinnamon. Like all of George Rico's cigars, the premium Gran Habano La Conquista is a remarkable bargain for any enthusiast looking to take their smoking game to the next level. With a generous 24 sticks loaded into each box, just think of them as long-term investments in your daily enjoyment. Don't worry, we'll be here waiting when you need to re-up sooner than expected.

With all due pomp and circumstance as befits such royally delicious cigars, let us introduce you to the Persian King Natural and Maduro . Brought to you by Gran Habano’s Guillermo and George Rico , you can be assured the famous father and son duo have spared no effort in crafting a stogie that is set to rule the mid-priced cigar empire. To accomplish this coronation, the Rico’s have recruited a variety of the lushest aged Nicaraguan tobaccos to come together in blended harmony. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) Persian King Natural: As though a paper band carrying its frontmark were beneath it, the Persian King Natural instead identifies itself with a bright and golden strip of pigtailed Connecticut Shade tobacco that decorates the foot in stark color contrast to the rich brown Habano which coats the rest of each stout vitola. The scents and flavors of a cold draw are reminiscent of cedar, cocoa, and hay, but a flame releases the cigar’s true majesty. A sweet grassiness awakens the palate, a delightful taste soon to be expanded with loamy earth, oak, black pepper, cream, cinnamon, and plum. Persian King Maduro: The gleaming and uniformly dark Maduro wrapper that graces each solid vitola needs no band to signal its sovereign nature, but what good is a fancy cloak if it doesn’t have some decoration? Instead of a trimmed foot or even the shaggy tobacco you’ll occasionally see, the foot of each Persian King Maduro is closed with an inch-wide strip of light brown tobacco which is pigtailed into a fancy coil. Very stylish. Clipping both ends reveals a well-packed core while a flame brings forth a wealth of rich flavor. Earth and oak and cocoa in spades, but behind these bold elements quietly sit walnut, toasted oats, cinnamon, malt, and cherry stem ready to engage the wise palate. Full-flavored and full-bodied from start to finish, you may want to kneel while enjoying this regal stick if you’re not already kicked back in your favorite chair. Come visit the court of the Persian King, and reap the benefits of Gran Habano’s commitment to flavor and quality that won’t cost you a king’s ransom. Go for the glory by buying a full box of fifty, but if your castle can’t quite hold that many we do carry them in five packs and singles. Either way, you’ll feel like a monarch each time you light one up.

Persian Queen is the long-awaited offshoot of Persian King, the rustic value-priced cigar from the father and son team of George and Guillermo Rico of Gran Habano. Hailing from Honduras and limited in production to just 500 boxes of 50 cigars, Persian Queen is rather special in that it is a true limited edition. Not only that, but it is also draped in two different wrapper leaves in barber pole fashion, making it as beautiful in appearance as it is delicious. For the blend, the binder and filler tobacco are from Nicaragua and the two wrappers are Ecuadorian Connecticut and Nicaraguan Corojo. The result of this blend is a medium-bodied masterpiece suitable for cigar freaks of all calibers. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) The box is plain and simple, and the cigars wear no bands. Each stick is lovingly constructed and rolled with precision. The result being a seamless barber pole cigar with an unfinished foot. The draw is highly productive, offering plentiful opportunities to take in all the wonderful flavor and aroma produced by this exciting blend. Immediately upon lighting up, a quick burst of cedar and white pepper, started things off. Soon, notes of bread and cereal oddly form the core of the flavor profile, surrounded by an earthy aroma and crisp raw tobacco flavor, likely coming from the Connecticut side of the wrapper. The puffs are creamy and smooth, and the finish is short and clean. Persian Queen ends up residing as a true medium-bodied cigar. Tasty, enjoyable, versatile, and suitable for all audiences. Persian Queen is a cigar for everyone. The price to quality ratio is amazing, especially for a limited production stick. Its flavor profile is simple, yet interesting, and its medium body pairs well with white wine, light beers, or any decent whiskey. If you tried the Persian King back in the day, or simply are a fan of George Rico's other projects such as La Conquista or Gran Habano Vintage 2002 , you should give Persian Queen a try. We live in a time when prices are going up on everything, including cigars. How refreshing it is to know that there are cigars like Persian Queen out there that combine quality and value and can be enjoyed by just about anyone! Long live the queen!

When George Rico introduced the Gran Habano Corojo #5, the cigar world rejoiced in its full-flavored and bodied taste. It is hard to believe this stick could get any better, but the Gran Habano Vintage 2002 does just that. Not only is the blend improved with the introduction of an aged Corojo wrapper from 2002 but the price is much easier to look at as well. This medium-to-full-bodied cigar is perfect for anyone to try, whether you love heavier sticks, or you are looking to step up your flavor profile. (Shop other Gran Habano Cigars ) These super-oily dark and rich Nicaraguan Corojo 2002 wrapped beauties are packed to the gills with Cuban seed long filler tobacco from the finest fields in Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. These sticks are chock full of hearty nutty flavors balanced with notes of cream, coffee and dirt making this a medium-to-full-bodied blend that nearly everybody will enjoy. The construction is flawless as one would expect from a George Rico cigar, and despite the price, the flavors match up with some of the much higher cost cigars on the market, even ones from Gran Habano themselves At such a low price per stick, people will be hard to find a cigar that is this flavorful, this well made, and this cost effective. You can even fool your friends at your next herf by making them think you are passing out much higher priced sticks. Given the heavy nature of the smoke it is best enjoyed after a good meal with a nice glass of red wine or a stout which can hold up to the flavors.

Gurkha owner Kaizad Hansotia dates the name being associated with cigars back 125 years, and for this incredible anniversary a special cigar was needed to celebrate. When Gurkha sets out to make a special stick, the eyes of the cigar world take notice. The 125th Anniversary Gurkha cigar is certainly something to celebrate. Named the 9th best cigar of 2013 by Cigar Aficionado, this standout cigar is made in the PDR factory in the Dominican Republic. A truly international blend of Nicaraguan, Brazilian, and Dominican filler tobaccos and bound with a Ecuadorian leaf and wrapped in a beautiful Brazilian wrapper. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) With a beautiful large Gurkha band embellished with gold and the 125th anniversary moniker on the side, you are sure to know you are in for a special smoke. While the Brazilian wrapper has a somewhat dry appearance, the construction was impeccable and there was no veining to speak of. Before lighting there is an almost citrus aroma of orange and this carried over to the flavor afterward. On top of this tantalizing note, there was also great tastes of leather and spice. 125 years in the cigar industry is something to be very Proud of, and Gurkha has made a perfect cigar to celebrate. Gurkha's 125 Anniversary cigar is an amazing medium-to-full smoke with very complex flavors and fantastic construction. These citrus notes pair wonderfully with a nice gin and tonic on the deck as you forget about the day and wonder what the next will bring.

If you've been casting about for a unique and flavorful cigar to break you out of a smoking rut, then the Gurkha Barracuda is going to be a prize catch. Loaded to the gills with the kinds of flavorful tobacco they're known for, this latest creation from K. Hansotia and his talented team is a medium to full-strength ocean of delight. Rolled with utmost skill into one of the most difficult vitolas around, a 6" x 56 Double Perfecto, the Barracuda contains a wealth of Honduran longleaf aged to shimmering perfection beneath a sturdy and aromatic Honduran binder. An appropriately toothy and oily Habano wrapper finishes each stick, transforming it into a sleek and impressive trophy. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Flooding the senses from the moment it's hoisted from a humidor, a weighty and aromatic Gurkha Barracuda cigar sits in the hand with bottomless potential. The scents of chocolate and crisp tobacco lead to flavors of cocoa and mild spice, causing the hands to scramble for a lighter. A wide net is cast by each thick perfecto to bring together a school of complimentary tastes, from rich and woody cedar to semi-sweet stone fruit. There's some black coffee with just the right touch of bitterness, a tasted nuttiness brought out in the retrohale, and a warm nutmeg and cinnamon finish so delicious that you'll want to mount it over your fireplace. Get a bundle of Gurkha Barracuda today and prepare for a rush of excitement and anticipation. No worries though, because we'll get them to you safe and secure in no time flat. By this time next week, you'll be bragging to all of your buddies about landing the deal of a lifetime for a monster of a cigar, and since you'll be passing them around at the same time they'll know the tale is true.

One can imagine that naming a cigar is a difficult task in trying to find just the right balance between symbolic and memorable, but it must have been the easiest thing in the world to come up with the moniker 'Gurkha Beast.' Picture a small man sitting at a desk tasked with creatively labeling each of K. Hansotia's numerous latest creations when a huge, 6" x 60 ring gauge monstrosity lands before him with an earth-shaking thud. After picking himself up off the floor, he notices the expansive foot crammed with Nicaraguan, Dominican, and Honduran tobaccos beneath a Dominican binder, the ancient and rare 8-year-aged Costa Rican Maduro wrapper, and it hits him. Beast. This cigar is a Beast. Drained and exhausted from the effort, he feels it is time to knock off early and enjoy a cold cerveza in the Nicaraguan sunshine after a job well done. Now it is the smoker's turn to do battle. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) When you grab hold of a Gurkha Beast, you had better grip it tightly. Otherwise, this dark and ominous Super Toro is going to eat your lunch. With an oily, toothy outer skin the color of water-stained leather, each weighty stick exudes an earthy aroma, while the cold draw through the densely packed core carries a touch of sweet stone fruit. Once you wrestle the Beast with a sturdy flame, it will slowly fight back with thick clouds of smoke heavy with espresso and spice, dark berries and cedar. As the fire rages slowly towards your waiting maw over a two-hour burn time, expect a flavorful release of creamy cedar and leather, along with a raw molasses finish that keeps the medium-full strength from going completely out of control.

Gurkha Beauty is the cigar that was released to complement the ever-popular Beast in the recent lineup from Gurkha. Hailing from Honduras, the Gurkha Beauty is lovingly crafted with a 5-year-aged blend of filler and binder tobaccos from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. It is finished off with a gorgeous Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. This is one heck of a gorgeous mild-bodied stick that is a must-try for any Gurkha fan. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Always an easy draw and always a razor-sharp burn, Gurkha Beauty gives off massive amounts of silky white smoke. This stick treats the palate to a smooth, creamy flavor profile of sweet tobacco with hints of nutmeg and cedar. A bit of spice on the finish is the icing on the cake, and this cigar only gets better as it is smoked. Any connoisseur can enjoy the complex, mild flavors of the Gurkha Beauty. It is a high-end cigar aimed at a high-end crowd of discriminating aficionados that don't just want any mild cigar, but rather a mild cigar with a little something extra. It pairs nicely with champagne and can be compared to Montecristo and AVO Heritage . This lovely work of art, like many top-shelf cigars, can be described with words like luxury, elegance, and of course, beauty.

Gurkha Cask Blend cigars are classified by K. Hansotia as one of Gurkha's 'signature' smokes, indicating that they embody the best qualities the brand is known for. It means excellent construction. Exquisite flavor. Supreme value. Yes we said value, which is a word not often associated with the company responsible for some of the world's most expensive cigars. But here's why: Where else can you find a full 100-count box of uber-premium sticks, all of which utilize a secret blend of rich and sultry tobaccos to create a medium-bodied masterpiece, for less than expected? It's madness of the best kind. You're wondering if it's worth it, aren't you? (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Well hell yes it is! Each Gurkha Cask Blend cigar exudes an impressive leathery aroma and glossy sheen. Rolled at the family-owned Tabacalera Las Lavas in the Dominican Republic, the utmost care and attention to detail has been applied to each cigar to provide the perfect smoking experience. From the first smooth puff to the last creamy draw, your only concern will be maximizing the time left to enjoy the toasty goodness full of roasted coffee, walnut and semi-sweet chocolate backed by touches of cinnamon and a whisper of mint. Good thing they're slow burners.

Setting out to create a cigar with some of the finest, rarest, and well-aged tobaccos. Kaizad Hansotia made Cellar Reserve. These cigars utilize a filler blend that is all Dominican tobacco that has been aged for 15-years and are wrapped in a gorgeous oily Criollo 1998 wrapper. These cigars sit firmly in the medium body range. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Gurkha Cellar Reserve will have your mouth watering from the moment the wrapper hits your lips. The natural oils of the leaf will bring on a sweet peppery taste that only intensifies throughout the whole smoking experience. With a nice smooth finish, this cigar is full of flavor. Gurkha Cellar Reserve can be a pretty hard to find cigar. This exclusive stick is made with some of the best tobaccos out there and the flavors confirm that. Pick up a box today, while they are available.

Another year, another new and great smoke from Gurkha with the Cellar Reserve 21 Year cigar. One might begin to get suspicious about how K. Hansotia and Co. can keep churning out such fine vitolas packed with tobaccos of extraordinary quality, but it doesn't matter as long as the taste is there. And there it is in spades. When the blend carries at its core a choice selection of Dominican longleaf allowed to age and mellow for twenty-one long years (what, did you doubt the name?), the result is an experience unlike any other. Add to this a hefty amount of fine Nicaraguan tobacco and a silky Connecticut shade wrapper tailor-made for enjoyment and this cigar is a force to be reckoned with. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) You like figurados, with their tapered feet and pointy heads, don't you? Admit it, there's just something ultimately perfect about the hard-to-roll shape that somehow defines your impression of the ideal cigar. Luckily, with the Gurkha Cellar Reserve 21 Year, you'll have plenty of time to admire the time and effort spent in creating such a work of art. This is because each stick burns slowly and true, pouring layer after layer of sweet cream and cedar and black pepper and orange peel and nutmeg onto the salivating palate. Make sure not to rush and to take a sip of your beverage every now and again, because patience will be rewarded as you squeeze every drop of deliciousness from this medium-bodied delight. Despite a reputation for sky-high MSRP, Gurkha has wisely priced the Cellar Reserve 21 Year to be within reach of the average Joe. While it might not be a daily treat for everyone, there are undoubtedly plenty of 'special occasions' every month to justify keeping more than a few on hand for when the need arises. You might even want to share it with your friends. The good ones, at least.

You know, K. Hansotia had something up his sleeve when he named the Gurkha Cellar Reserve Edicion Especial cigar. For all of the limited or unique or uber-expensive smokes he has released, it makes the inquisitive aficionado wonder what makes this particular stick so 'especial'. Lucky for us, the answer is easy to understand: the tobacco. Each stout figurado in the line is filled to the brim with some of the finest Dominican longleaf imaginable, including a hefty portion of 18-year-old tobacco that provides an extremely smooth experience despite the power which develops while the toothy Corojo wrapper slowly burns. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Resplendent in its detailed orange and gold band, the 5" x 58 Gurkha Cellar Reserve Edicion Especial perfecto smells of leather and fresh hay, and tastes of cocoa and graham during the cold draw test. Easily lit, the tapered foot teases the palate with vanilla and baking spices, but the flavor really blossoms as the full width of the cigar's body is reached. The taste of freshly roasted black coffee fills the billowing smoke, followed closely by loamy earth and cedar. A lush berry-like sweetness rides on top of potent dark cocoa as the middle third is reached, with black pepper tempered by sweet cream during the cool burning final stages. Ready for immediate enjoyment by experienced smokers, we wouldn't want to discourage more novice enthusiasts from grabbing a few of these delightful sticks. While certainly tilting to the heavier side in terms of strength, the well-aged tobacco does keep the Gurkha Cellar Reserve Edicion Especial from being bitter or harsh, so it makes for a treat with a stiff drink after a hearty meal for just about everyone. Mmmmmm. Delicious.

Gurkha Cellar Reserve Limitada is an extension of the amazing yet rare Cellar Reserve line. With the same 15 year old rare Dominican tobacco as the filler, this version includes a dark and sweet Brazilian Arapiraca Maduro wrapper. This wrapper intensifies the flavor a little more and adds some body to the still very smooth cigar. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) The dark wrapper on Gurkha Cellar Reserve Limitada brings additional sweetness to your lips along with the naturally smooth yet earthy core of filler tobacco. This makes this one of the more complex Gurkha cigars on the market. As you get to the final third of this cigar, a peppery spice begins to develop but never overpowers all the other wonderful flavors previously experienced.

Gurkha Regent is one of the most iconic cigars Gurkha president Kaizad Hansotia has ever cooked up. After sinking below the radar for a short period, Regent has now been re-blended and re-introduced using Dominican filler and Indonesian binder tobaccos that earned it a 90 rating in its early days. The cigar is finished with a very special Habano 2000 wrapper from Honduras. This modestly-priced masterpiece will impress anyone that can appreciate a well-rounded top-shelf cigar.(See all Gurkha Cigars ) Massive bursts of smoke bombard the taste buds with a rich, earthy profile speckled with hints here and there of cherry and cinnamon. Chocolate and a faint coffee taste linger in the background. The medium-bodied Gurkha Regent was originally intended for serious connoisseurs, but at these prices, anyone and everyone not only can, but SHOULD dive in and try one. It pairs very well with bourbon and the taste profile can be compared to Nica Libre and Obsidian White Noise. For a very satisfying smoke with all the luxuries that come from Gurkha, but without the luxury price tag, grab some Gurkha Regents and live the high life in style!

Legacy blends from Gurkha tend to disappear as often as two more show up to take its place, but the Gurkha Crest cigar has aged gracefully into one of the brand's top selling frontmarks. Released by K. Hansotia in 2008, this medium strength yet full bodied smoke is loaded with everything the discriminating enthusiast has been hunting for whether they realize it or not. There's the sultry Connecticut Broadleaf that covers each stick, truly a shining beacon of quality and class. Premium longleaf tobaccos from Nicaragua lurk just below the surface, ready to fire off a volley of deliciousness straight to the eager palate. Add to this a price that's tough to beat, from a brand known for high MSRPs no less, and we've got a winner. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Each Gurkha Crest might as well be a cigar-shaped doughnut dipped in perfectly tempered dark chocolate for as glossy and oily as it appears, plus the aroma from the unlit stick will do nothing to dissuade from this impression. By the time the sweet cocoa and cream awaken during the opening of a newly lit stick, sitting alongside rich coffee and wheat toast, it's like having a second breakfast. The leather, cinnamon, and clove that arrive during the second third will bring the smoker to a place of complete satisfaction, while the earthy, peaty finale will leave you both relaxed and ready to conquer what remains of the day no matter if it's morning, noon, or night. Whether new to the brand or if you're ready to reacquaint yourself with Gurkha cigars now that their prices have come back down to Earth, there's really no better place to start than with the Gurkha Crest. Perfect as a high-end daily treat for the accomplished aficionado or a special occasion smoke for the exploring beginner, you'll thank yourself every time you light one up.

K. Hansotia is a master when it comes to blending cigars, and the Gurkha Elegance is proof of that. Always coming up with new blends and new lines, Gurkha is at the forefront of pushing the boundaries of what to expect in a cigar. The Elegance features a very rare 7-year-aged Connecticut wrapper that limits production to only 800 boxes a year. Underneath this wrapper are some of the finest Dominican fillers and a smooth Connecticut binder. This cigar checks in just a hair under a medium body. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) A Connecticut wrapper is the mildest of leaves chosen for this part of a cigar, but the age on the one used in the Elegance adds a perfect amount of creaminess to the stellar nutty characteristics of the filler tobacco. What starts out as extremely mild, grows in strength throughout the smoke, but never gets to the point of crossing over to a medium body. This is a prime example of how flavorful a milder cigar can be. The Gurkha Elegance is one of the most boutique lines from the famed brand due to the scarcity of the wrapper leaf. Mild enough to enjoy with a morning cup of coffee, this cigar is also flavorful enough to stand out after a nice dinner. If you are looking for something that will never overpower but will still make your taste buds sing, this is the cigar for you.

Do you believe in Ghosts? We don't know if we do or not, but one thing we do believe in is Gurkha's Ghost cigar. When a brand releases as many variants as Gurkha does, there can be a fear that they are spreading themselves too thin, but after lighting up a Gurkha Ghost, it is definite they truly put their all into every cigar they make. A wonderful medium-bodied cigar that is full of flavor, this is a stick not to fear but to embrace. Made in the Dominican Republic, this stick features a fantastic blend of Dominican and Nicaraguan filler with a Dominican Criollo 98 binder and a luxurious Brazilian Arapiraca maduro wrapper. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) The large Gurkha band is black and silver and perfectly accents the color of the wrapper. The dark Brazilian tobacco has a sheen to it and the oily nature made us excited to smoke it. The smell before match touched foot was one of cedar, and that carried on throughout the smoking experience. The first half of this cigar had an almost chocolate-like sweetness paired off with a nice pepper. After the initial puffs, these notes paired down and the body did as well. As with all Gurkhas, the construction was impeccable. The draw was fantastic, and the burn was perfect. Paranormal investigations seem to be all the rage these days, but you don't have to invest in all that extra equipment to find a great cigar. Gurkha Ghost will fit that bill nicely. From wrapper, to flavor, to construction, this is a great smoke for anyone who loves medium-bodied cigars. We enjoyed ours after dinner with a dark roast coffee, but could definitely enjoy this anytime of day. For another great cigar with a beautiful Brazilian wrapper, give the CAO Brazilia a try.

The cigar that started it all and represents the brand better than any other, the Gurkha Grand Reserve is the epitome of luxury, style, and good taste. For the inaugural launch of what would become one of the most well-known and widely traveled premium cigar brands on the planet, owner and mastermind K. Hansotia knew he had to create something special. For this he took expertly crafted cigars containing a three year old Dominican filler and binder overlaid with an exquisite six year old Connecticut wrapper and carefully infused them with Remy Martin Louis XIII cognac. We also offer the Gordo and the Churchill without the cognac and also without tubes. The result is a world-class cigar like no other. (See all Gurkha Cigars )

The Gurkha Heritage limited release edition is a medium-bodied cigar full of robust flavors, hand-rolled in Nicaragua and comes in a rare 35-count box. Blended by Gurkhas top cigar-smiths at American Caribbean Cigars in Nicaragua, t he flavorful blend has rich coffee and dark chocolate tones with a subtle and well-balanced spice present throughout. (See all Gurkha Cigars )

Gurkha Legend is a cigar that certainly lives up to its name, as it's probably the most famous of all that Gurkha has offered over the years, and that is no small statement. Made in the Dominican Republic under the supervision of renowned mastermind Kaizad Hansotia, Gurkha Legend is the epitome of all that Gurkha stands for. It has become synonymous with quality, value, and flavor, and has stood the test of time. Countless cigar connoisseurs have enjoyed it, many publications have raved about it. It is just a cigar for the ages, and that simply can't be refuted. Legend consists of a smooth blend of Dominican fillers inside a genuine Cameroon binder. The package is topped off with a golden Connecticut wrapper leaf, making a medium-bodied masterpiece that's both refined and unique. As if that was not enough, it is fascinating to note that the premium tobaccos used in Legend are aged no less than 8 full years for maximum smokability. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Gurkha Legend is constructed beautifully. Seamlessly rolled into shape and glistening with a natural sheen, each cigar almost appears as a bar of gold. Legend starts off with a slight peppery burst and quickly mellows to a medley of nutty, grassy flavors. Caramel, clove, and anise round out the flavor profile before transitioning to a smooth, creamy finish. It seriously is no wonder how this cigar has survived so long. While Gurkha Legend can undoubtedly impress even the most seasoned aficionados, it is suitable for just about anyone that loves fine cigars, even beginners. Medium-bodied and flavorful, it is no doubt enjoyable for any occasion. Legend pairs well with white or red wine, or a simple glass of whiskey. Other incredible sticks in the seemingly never-ending Gurkha portfolio include the infamous Beauty and the highly-rated Cellar Reserve series. Simple, refined, and downright enjoyable, Gurkha Legend is a cigar that will go down in history as exactly that: a true legend.

The Master Select line of Gurkha Cigars features wrappers made from extra-select six year-old vintage Habana 2000 tobacco. These are powerful and very complex cigars. (See all Gurkha Cigars ) Gurkha Cigar history: In 1989, Kaizad Hansotia decided to resurrect a cigar brand rich in tradition and steeped in legend and history. Gurkha cigars were created more than a century ago and were known for their meticulously and artisanaly handcrafted cigars, but when Hansotia revived the brand, there was no way he could have known that the cigar industry was about to experience a boom and he would have the perfect product to attract the new cigar consumer.
